definition_zh: 命名体系；命名法；（某一领域的）名称总集
definition_en: a system or set of names used consistently in a particular field, especially in science
core_image: 一间标本馆的抽屉全贴着统一格式的标签，每张标签只写一个名字，谁来看都能对上同一件东西
scene: 植物标本馆里，馆长指着一排标签说：Every specimen here must follow the same nomenclature.
sceneCN: 这里 nomenclature 指「某一领域统一使用的一整套命名体系」（第 1 个义项：为一个领域规定统一名称的系统）；句意是馆里每件标本都必须遵循同一套命名体系。

derivatives.zh: 命名体系的；命名法上的
命名者；（旧）报名字的侍从

senses.title: A naming system for a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域统一使用的命名体系
senses.definition: a system or set of names used consistently in a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域内统一使用的一整套名称
senses.example: Botanical nomenclature changes slowly because stability matters more than elegance.
senses.exampleCN: 植物命名体系变化很慢，因为稳定比优雅更重要。
senses.why: Nomen gives the word name and calare gives to call; a nomenclature is the whole way a field calls its objects, not a single name.
senses.whyCN: nomen 给出「名字」，calare 给出「呼叫」；nomenclature 是一个领域称呼其对象的整套方式，而不是单个名字。

senses.title: The act of assigning names
senses.titleCN: 给对象命名的行为
senses.definition: the process of giving names to things within a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域内为事物取名的过程
senses.example: The nomenclature of the new collection took the curators two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 给新藏品命名花了馆员两周时间。
senses.why: The same word can name the activity itself: to call things by name is exactly what the Latin phrase describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可指活动本身：按拉丁原义，「把名字叫出来」正是它字面描述的动作。

senses.title: The whole stock of names in a science
senses.titleCN: 某一学科积累下来的名称总集
senses.definition: the total set of names used in a science or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科或科目使用的全部名称
senses.example: Students of anatomy spend a term learning its nomenclature.
senses.exampleCN: 学解剖的学生要花一个学期学习它的名称总集。
senses.why: Once a system is written down, it becomes a body of names that learners must acquire as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 体系一旦写成文字，就变成学习者必须整体掌握的一整套名称。

senses.title: Technical vocabulary opaque to outsiders
senses.titleCN: 外人难懂的专业术语
senses.definition: the technical terms of a profession, often hard for outsiders to understand
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业的专业术语，外人往往难以理解
senses.example: The article was dense with legal nomenclature that general readers could not follow.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章满是法律术语，普通读者跟不上。
senses.why: A closed naming system doubles as a barrier: insiders call things correctly, while outsiders hear only labels.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的命名体系同时也是一道门槛：内行叫得准确，外行只听到一串标签。

senses.title: A formal code of naming rules
senses.titleCN: 规定如何命名的正式法规
senses.definition: an official set of rules governing how names are formed and used
senses.definitionCN: 规定名称如何构成与使用的正式规则
senses.example: The committee amended the nomenclature to settle a long dispute over mineral groups.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会修订命名法规，以平息关于矿物分组的长期争议。
senses.why: When many people name objects, a list needs law; the word shifts from inventory to rulebook.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共同为对象命名时，名单就需要规则；词义于是从「清单」转向「法规」。

senses.title: A catalogue or list of names
senses.titleCN: 成册的名称清单
senses.definition: a list or catalogue in which names are recorded
senses.definitionCN: 记录名称的清单或目录
senses.example: The archive keeps a nomenclature of every species recorded in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆保存着山谷中每一种已记录物种的名录。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a written list; a catalogue is simply the system made visible on paper.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是书面清单；名录只是把体系摊开在纸面上。

senses.title: The naming half of taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分类学中负责命名的那一半
senses.definition: the part of taxonomy that assigns and regulates names
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中负责分配与管理名称的部分
senses.example: Taxonomy has two halves: identification of specimens and nomenclature.
senses.exampleCN: 分类学有两半：鉴定标本与命名。
senses.why: Identification asks which thing this is; nomenclature asks what it must be called, a separate task.
senses.whyCN: 鉴定问的是「这是什么东西」，命名问的是「它必须叫什么」，这是两项独立的任务。

senses.title: A controlled set of labels in a database
senses.titleCN: 数据库中受控的标签体系
senses.definition: a standardized set of labels used to index records consistently
senses.definitionCN: 用于一致地索引记录的标准标签集
senses.example: The database maps every field to a controlled nomenclature so that searches do not miss records.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库把每个字段都映射到受控标签体系，使检索不会漏掉记录。
senses.why: Modern data work repeats the same gesture: fix one label per kind so that every record can be found.
senses.whyCN: 现代数据工作重复同一个动作：为每一类固定一个标签，使每条记录都能被找到。

intro.en: Nomenclature comes from Latin nomenclatura, literally a calling of names, built on nomen name and calare to call. The root is transparent; the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: nomenclature 来自拉丁 nomenclatura，字面是「把名字叫出来」，由 nomen「名字」与 calare「呼叫」构成。词根清楚，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Nomen meant name and is the source of nominal, nominate and misnomer; its Indo-European ancestor is reconstructed as *no-men-, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」，是 nominal、nominate、misnomer 的来源；其印欧语祖先被重构为 *no-men-，属于重构形式而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Calare meant to call, summon or proclaim; the caller was a calator, and the same verb lies behind calendar and the church word calends.
items.cn: calare 意为「呼叫、召来、宣告」；执行呼叫的人是 calator，同一个动词也出现在 calendar 与教会用语 calends 中。

items.en: Nomen plus calator produced nomenclatura, the act of calling names and, by extension, a list of names.
items.cn: nomen 加 calator 构成 nomenclatura，指呼名的动作，引申为名称清单。

items.en: English took the word in the early seventeenth century, first as a list or vocabulary of names rather than a formal scientific system.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪初借入这个词，最初指名称清单或名录，而非正式的科学体系。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to the naming systems of biology and chemistry, where rules decide which name is valid.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词被用于生物学与化学的命名体系，由规则决定哪个名称有效。

items.en: Source uncertain only as to the first date: the 1610s citation is an approximation, and intermediate forms differ between dictionaries; the nomen and calare roots themselves are not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定仅限首见年代：1610 年代的书证只是约数，各家词典给出的中间形式也不一致；nomen 与 calare 这两个词根本身并无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Latin name root but have drifted apart; group two holds near neighbours in the vocabulary of classification.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「名字」词根但语义已经分家的词；第二组是分类词汇中意思相近的词。

entries.definition: From nomen name: existing in name but not in fact; it shares the root without the sense of a naming system.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 nomen「名字」：只在名义上存在而非事实上存在；共享词根，但没有「命名体系」之义。

entries.definition: From nomen: to propose a person by name for a post; the naming here is a one-off act of proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 nomen：按名字提议某人担任某职；这里的命名只是一次性的提名动作。

entries.definition: Mis- wrongly plus nomen: a name that does not fit the thing, so it concerns one bad label rather than a whole system.
entries.definitionCN: mis-「错误」加 nomen：与事物不符的名称，因此说的是单个错误标签，而不是整套体系。

entries.definition: The Latin agent noun for one who calls names; in modern usage a person who compiles a specialized list of names.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中「呼名者」的施事名词；现代指编纂专业名称表的人。

entries.definition: The vocabulary of a field, with attention to the terms and their meanings rather than to the rules for assigning them.
entries.definitionCN: 某一领域的词汇，关注术语及其含义，而不关注分配名称的规则。

entries.definition: The entire science of grouping organisms; nomenclature is only its naming component.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物进行分组的整门科学；命名体系只是其中负责命名的一部分。

entries.definition: The act of sorting things into classes; it comes before naming and does not itself fix the names.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分入类别的动作；它先于命名，本身并不确定名称。

entries.definition: An alphabetized list of terms with explanations; a nomenclature may take this form but need not explain anything.
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排列并附解释的术语表；命名体系可以采用这种形式，但不必作任何解释。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Nomen name plus calare to call: a system that calls every object by an agreed name.
normal.cn: nomen「名字」加 calare「呼叫」：一套按约定名称呼叫每个对象的体系。

normal.en: The family runs nomenclature, nomenclatural, nomenclator and nomenclatorial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nomenclature、nomenclatural、nomenclator 与 nomenclatorial。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: botanical, zoological and chemical nomenclature.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：植物命名法、动物命名法、化学命名法。

normal.en: A nomenclature committee is a rule-making body, which shows the code sense.
normal.cn: 命名委员会是制定规则的机构，这体现了「法规」这一义项。

normal.en: Stability is the design goal: names change slowly so that records stay findable.
normal.cn: 稳定是设计目标：名称变化很慢，记录才能一直找得到。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of drawers, each carrying one label and nothing else.
abstract.cn: 想象一整墙抽屉，每只只贴一个标签，别的一概不写。

abstract.en: Picture a profession speaking its own dialect that outsiders cannot enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行业说着自己的方言，外人进不去。

abstract.en: Picture a map legend that every reader agrees to read the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图的图例，每位读者都同意按同一种方式去读。

examples.en: Zoological nomenclature requires that the first published name has priority.
examples.cn: 动物命名法规定，最早发表的名称享有优先权。

examples.en: Chemical nomenclature lets a reader infer the structure from the name alone.
examples.cn: 化学命名法让读者只凭名称就能推断结构。

examples.en: The new catalogue follows the nomenclature used by the national herbarium.
examples.cn: 新目录采用国家标本馆所用的命名体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nomen 名字 + calare 呼叫」——把名字一套套叫出来 → 命名体系、命名法

root: 拉丁 nomenclatura「呼名；名称清单」= nomen「名字」+ calare「呼叫」（呼名者 calator）；英语先指名录，后指学科命名体系。词根清楚，仅首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: a field decides how to call its objects, and that decision becomes a list, a rulebook, a closed dialect and finally a set of labels in a database.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个领域决定如何称呼它的对象，这一决定先成为清单，再成为法规、封闭的行话，最后成为数据库里的受控标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field agrees on one label for every object, so that everyone points to the same thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个领域为每个对象约定同一个标签，使所有人指向同一件东西。

branches.en: FIELD SYSTEM: a science needs one agreed way of calling every object it studies.
branches.cn: 领域体系：一门科学需要一种约定方式来称呼它研究的每个对象。

branches.en: THE ACT: naming is the event that creates the list in the first place.
branches.cn: 命名动作：命名正是最初造出这份清单的事件。

branches.en: CLOSED DIALECT: shared names turn into a language that outsiders cannot enter.
branches.cn: 封闭方言：共享的名称变成外人进不去的语言。

branches.en: LAW OF NAMES: a code decides which name is valid when several compete.
branches.cn: 名称之法：当多个名称竞争时，法规决定哪一个有效。

branches.en: VISIBLE LIST: from a paper catalogue to a database field, the system appears as labels in a row.
branches.cn: 可见清单：从纸质名录到数据库字段，体系都表现为一排标签。

intro.en: Nomenclature is a Latin compound whose two parts also build other English words, so the whole family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: nomenclature 是一个拉丁复合词，两部分还构成其他英语词，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen gives nominal, nominate and misnomer; Latin calare gives calendar and the agent noun calator, which combines with nomen in nomenclatura.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nomen 衍生 nominal、nominate 与 misnomer；拉丁 calare 衍生 calendar 及施事名词 calator，后者与 nomen 组合成 nomenclatura。

items.example: Nomen is the shared source of several English words about naming.
items.exampleCN: nomen 是若干关于命名的英语词的共同来源。

items.example: The verb described calling someone by name.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述的是按名字把人叫来。

items.example: The calator called each guest by name.
items.exampleCN: 呼名者逐个叫出客人的名字。

items.meaning: a calling of names; a list of names
items.example: The Latin noun already carried both the act and the list.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已同时包含动作与清单两义。

items.meaning: a system or list of names
items.example: Every specimen follows the same nomenclature.
items.exampleCN: 每件标本都遵循同一套命名体系。

items.example: The nomenclatural rules were revised last year.
items.exampleCN: 命名规则去年被修订。

items.meaning: a compiler or caller of names
items.example: The nomenclator checked every label in the archive.
items.exampleCN: 名称编纂者核对了档案里的每个标签。

items.meaning: relating to the work of naming
items.example: The paper discussed nomenclatorial practice in mineralogy.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文讨论了矿物学中的命名实务。

items.example: The nominal fee was never collected.
items.exampleCN: 那笔名义费用从未收取。

items.example: Calling it a lake is a misnomer, since it is a marsh.
items.exampleCN: 把它叫作湖是名称不当，因为它其实是沼泽。

latinEntries.meaning: a calling of names; a list of names

definition_zh: 二项式的；双名的；由两个名称（项）组成的；二项式
definition_en: consisting of two terms or two names; a mathematical expression with two terms
core_image: 一块牌子正面写属名、背面写种名，两半合起来才是一个完整称呼
scene: 数学课上，老师在黑板上写下两个项后说：This binomial can be expanded with a simple formula.
sceneCN: 这里 binomial 指「由两项组成的代数式」（第 1 个义项：含两个项的数学表达式）；句意是这个二项式可以用一个简单公式展开。

pos.zh: 二项式的；双名的；由两项组成的

forms.label: 形容词异体（生物学常用）

senses.title: An algebraic expression with two terms
senses.titleCN: 含两个项的代数式
senses.definition: a mathematical expression consisting of two terms connected by a plus or minus sign
senses.definitionCN: 由两个项以加号或减号连接的数学表达式
senses.example: The expression x plus y is the simplest binomial.
senses.exampleCN: 表达式 x 加 y 是最简单的二项式。
senses.why: Bi- means two and the -nomial part comes from nomen name; in algebra the two names are simply the two terms that the expression carries.
senses.whyCN: bi- 意为「二」，-nomial 部分来自 nomen「名字」；在代数里，这两个「名字」就是表达式所携带的两个项。

senses.title: A two-part biological name
senses.titleCN: 由两部分构成的生物学名
senses.definition: a scientific name made of a genus name followed by a species name
senses.definitionCN: 由属名加种名构成的学名
senses.example: Homo sapiens is a binomial that every biology student meets early.
senses.exampleCN: Homo sapiens 是每个生物学生很早就接触到的双名。
senses.why: Taxonomy gives each species two names joined into one label, so the mathematical word for two terms was borrowed for two name parts.
senses.whyCN: 分类学给每个物种两个名字并合成一个标签，于是数学里表示「两项」的词被借来表示「两个名称部分」。

senses.title: Consisting of two terms or names
senses.titleCN: 由两项或两个名称组成的
senses.definition: having or using two terms, names or parts
senses.definitionCN: 具有或使用两个项、名称或部分的
senses.example: The catalogue uses a binomial label for each species.
senses.exampleCN: 目录为每个物种使用一个双名标签。
senses.why: The adjective simply states the count: whatever the field, two elements are being joined into one unit.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是陈述数量：无论在哪个领域，都是把两个要素合成一个单位。

senses.title: A two-outcome statistical model
senses.titleCN: 只有两种结果的统计模型
senses.definition: describing a statistical experiment or distribution with exactly two possible outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 描述恰好有两种可能结果的统计实验或分布
senses.example: A coin toss is modelled as a binomial experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 抛硬币被建模为二项实验。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the two-part structure but applies it to outcomes: success or failure, heads or tails.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了「两部分」的结构，却把它用在结果上：成功或失败、正面或反面。

senses.title: The two-term polynomial as an object
senses.titleCN: 作为一个数学对象的二项多项式
senses.definition: a polynomial that contains exactly two terms
senses.definitionCN: 恰好含两个项的多项式
senses.example: In this chapter every binomial is written in descending powers.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一章里，每个二项式都按降幂书写。
senses.why: Used as a noun, the word points at the object itself rather than at its property of having two terms.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指向对象本身，而不是它「有两个项」这一属性。

senses.title: A two-element combination in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指由两个要素构成的组合
senses.definition: a combination or pairing of exactly two elements
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由两个要素构成的组合或配对
senses.example: The study treats nature and nurture as a binomial, not as rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把先天与后天当作一个双项组合，而非对立的两方。
senses.why: Outside mathematics the word can label any paired structure, because the two-part frame is what the speaker wants to stress.
senses.whyCN: 在数学之外，这个词可标记任何成对结构，因为说话者要强调的正是「两部分」这个框架。

senses.title: A two-word compound expression
senses.titleCN: 由两个词构成的复合表达
senses.definition: a fixed expression built from two words that function as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 由两个词构成、整体起一个单位作用的固定表达
senses.example: The term red fox is a binomial in ordinary descriptive writing.
senses.exampleCN: “红狐”这一说法在普通描写文中是一个双词组合。
senses.why: Linguists borrow the word when a two-word label behaves like a single name, echoing the taxonomic pattern.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用这个词，是指一个双词标签像单个名称那样起作用，与分类学的模式相呼应。

senses.title: A Latin-form two-part name on a label
senses.titleCN: 标签上以拉丁形式书写的双名
senses.definition: the Latin-form two-part name printed on a specimen or collection label
senses.definitionCN: 印在标本或藏品标签上的拉丁形式双名
senses.example: The curator corrected the binomial on the label before the exhibition opened.
senses.exampleCN: 展览开幕前，馆员更正了标签上的双名。
senses.why: In museum work the abstract system turns into ink: a binomial is what you actually read on the little card.
senses.whyCN: 在博物馆工作中，抽象体系变成墨迹：双名就是你真正在那张小卡片上读到的东西。

intro.en: Binomial comes from Late Latin binomius having two names, built on bini two each and nomen name; the mathematical use spread through French in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: binomial 来自晚期拉丁 binomius「有两个名字」，由 bini「各两个」与 nomen「名字」构成；数学用法在 16 世纪经法语传播。

items.en: Bini meant two each or in pairs, from bis twice; it marks the count of two rather than the act of naming.
items.cn: bini 意为「各两个、成对」，来自 bis「两次」；它标记的是数量二，而不是命名动作。

items.en: Nomen meant name and supplies the second element; the same root appears in nomenclature and misnomer.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」，提供第二个成分；同一词根出现在 nomenclature 与 misnomer 中。

items.en: Bini plus nomen produced binomius, having two names, an adjective used for things described by a pair of terms.
items.cn: bini 加 nomen 构成 binomius「有两个名字的」，用于以两个词来描述的事物。

items.en: French binôme named the two-term algebraic expression in the sixteenth century, and English borrowed the word in the 1550s.
items.cn: 法语 binôme 在 16 世纪指含两个项的代数式，英语于 16 世纪中叶借入。

items.en: Biology later applied the same adjective to names in two parts, and binomial nomenclature became the standard phrase in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 生物学后来把同一形容词用于由两部分构成的名称，binomial nomenclature 在 19 世纪成为标准说法。

items.en: Source partly uncertain: the nomen root is clear, but some accounts derive the mathematical term from Greek nomos part rather than Latin nomen; that Greek link is a hypothesis, and the first date of the biological sense is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源部分不确定：nomen 词根清楚，但有些说法认为数学术语来自希腊 nomos「部分」而非拉丁 nomen；这一希腊语联系只是假说，生物义的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look alike because of the bi- prefix but descend from different roots; group two holds words close in meaning within algebra and naming.
note.cn: 第一组是因 bi- 前缀而形近、却来自不同词根的同形词；第二组是代数与命名范围内意思相近的词。

entries.definition: Bi- two plus annus year: happening every two years, so the bi- is shared but the root is annus, not nomen.
entries.definitionCN: bi-「二」加 annus「年」：每两年发生一次，因此 bi- 相同而词根是 annus，并非 nomen。

entries.definition: Bi- plus latus side: involving two sides, which shows the same prefix over a different root.
entries.definitionCN: bi- 加 latus「边」：涉及两侧，说明同一前缀可接不同词根。

entries.definition: From Latin binarius of two: made of two parts or using two digits; it is closer in sense to binomial than to nomen words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 binarius「二的」：由两部分构成或使用两个数字；在语义上比 nomen 词族更接近 binomial。

entries.definition: A later variant of binomial used mainly in biology for two-part names; the two forms differ in spelling, not in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: binomial 的后起异体，主要用于生物学的双名；两种形式只差拼写，意义相同。

entries.definition: The three-term counterpart of a binomial, built with tri- three; naming follows the same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: binomial 的三项对应词，由 tri-「三」构成；构词方式相同。

entries.definition: An expression with a single term; it marks the lower end of the same series.
entries.definitionCN: 只含一个项的表达式；它标出同一序列的下限。

entries.definition: An expression with one or more terms, of which a binomial is the special case with exactly two.
entries.definitionCN: 含一个或多个项的表达式，二项式是其中恰好两项的特例。

entries.definition: The formal two-part name of an organism; it is what a binomial denotes in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 生物正式的两部分名称；在生物学中正是 binomial 所指的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Bi- two plus nomen name: a form that carries two names or two terms.
normal.cn: bi-「二」加 nomen「名字」：一个携带两个名字或两个项的形式。

normal.en: Algebra keeps the family: binomial, trinomial, monomial, polynomial.
normal.cn: 代数保留了这个词族：二项式、三项式、单项式、多项式。

normal.en: Binomial theorem, binomial coefficient and binomial distribution are fixed companions.
normal.cn: 二项式定理、二项式系数、二项分布是固定搭配。

normal.en: In biology the two parts are genus and species, written side by side.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，两部分是属名与种名，并排书写。

normal.en: The same word covers a sum and a name, because both come in twos.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指和式也指名称，因为两者都以「二」为结构。

abstract.en: Picture a sign with two halves that only read correctly when joined.
abstract.cn: 想象一块牌子分成两半，只有拼起来才读得通。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of boots: useless alone, a unit together.
abstract.cn: 想象一双靴子：单只没用，成对才是一个单位。

abstract.en: Picture a two-panel window that frames one view.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇双格窗，两格框住同一片景。

examples.en: The tutor asked the class to square the binomial without expanding every term.
examples.cn: 导师让全班在不逐项展开的情况下求这个二项式的平方。

examples.en: Each newly described beetle received a binomial in the museum register.
examples.cn: 每只新描述的甲虫都在博物馆登记册里获得一个双名。

examples.en: The binomial test is appropriate when every trial has only two outcomes.
examples.cn: 当每次试验只有两种结果时，适合使用二项检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bi 两 + nomen 名字」——两个名字或两个项合在一起 → 双名、二项式

root: 晚期拉丁 binomius「有两个名字的」= bini「各两个」+ nomen「名字」；数学义经法语 binôme 进入英语。词根清楚；希腊 nomos 之说仅为假说，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one frame: two elements joined into one unit, whether the elements are algebraic terms, name parts, outcomes or words.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用同一个框架：两个要素合成一个单位，无论这两个要素是代数项、名称部分、结果还是词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single label built from two halves, neither of which is complete alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个由两半构成的标签，任何一半单独都不完整。

branches.en: ALGEBRAIC OBJECT: two terms joined by a sign form one expression that can be handled as a unit.
branches.cn: 代数对象：两个项由符号连接成一个可按单位处理的表达式。

branches.en: NAME LABEL: genus plus species, or the ink on a specimen card, is one name in two parts.
branches.cn: 名称标签：属名加种名，或标本卡上的墨迹，都是分作两部分的同一个名称。

branches.en: COUNTING PROPERTY: the adjective simply says that exactly two parts are present.
branches.cn: 数量属性：形容词只是说明恰好存在两个部分。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: statistics applies the two-part frame to success and failure.
branches.cn: 两种结果：统计学把两部分框架用在成功与失败上。

branches.en: PAIRED STRUCTURE: any two-element pairing or two-word label can borrow the word.
branches.cn: 成对结构：任何双要素配对或双词标签都可借用这个词。

intro.en: Binomial is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun, and both parts recur in other English words, so the word can be read as two morphemes.
intro.cn: binomial 由一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁名词构成，两部分都重现于其他英语词，因此可按两个语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis and bini give bi- and binary; Latin nomen gives nominal, nominate, misnomer and nomenclature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis 与 bini 给出 bi- 与 binary；拉丁 nomen 给出 nominal、nominate、misnomer 与 nomenclature。

items.example: The prefix marks a count of two in many English words.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多英语词中标出数量二。

items.example: Nomen is the source of several words about naming.
items.exampleCN: nomen 是若干关于命名的词的来源。

items.meaningCN: 有两个名称或两个项的
items.example: This binomial can be expanded with a formula.
items.exampleCN: 这个二项式可以用一个公式展开。

items.example: The binominal label was printed in italics.
items.exampleCN: 双名标签用斜体印出。
这些数据呈二项分布。
二进制编码使用两个数字。
植物命名体系遵循一部法规。

items.example: The old name proved to be a misnomer.
items.exampleCN: 那个旧名称被证明是名称不当。

items.example: A trinomial has one more term than a binomial.
items.exampleCN: 三项式比二项式多一个项。

definition_zh: 双名命名法；双名命名体系；由一个属名加一个种名构成的学名
definition_en: the biological system of giving each species a two-part Latin name, or such a name itself
core_image: 一株植物只挂一块牌子，牌上并排两个拉丁词，第一个指属，第二个指种
scene: 在植物园的名牌前，讲解员指着牌子说：Binomial nomenclature gives every species a two-part name.
sceneCN: 这里 binomial nomenclature 指「给每个物种一个两段式学名的生物命名体系」（第 1 个义项：林奈式双名命名法）；句意是双名命名法给每个物种一个由两部分组成的名称。

pos.zh: 双名命名法；双名命名体系

collocations.zh: 植物学中的双名命名法

senses.title: The Linnaean system of two-part names
senses.titleCN: 林奈式的两段式命名体系
senses.definition: the biological system in which every species receives a two-part Latin name
senses.definitionCN: 给每个物种一个两段式拉丁学名的生物命名体系
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature replaced long descriptive phrases with stable two-word labels.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法用稳定的双词标签取代了冗长的描述性短语。
senses.why: Binomial supplies the two-part frame and nomenclature the whole system; together they name the practice that Linnaeus made standard.
senses.whyCN: binomial 提供「两部分」的框架，nomenclature 提供「整套体系」；合起来就是林奈使之标准化的那套做法。

senses.title: An actual two-part scientific name
senses.titleCN: 一个具体的两段式学名
senses.definition: a particular species name consisting of a genus name and a species epithet
senses.definitionCN: 由属名与种加词构成的某个具体物种名称
senses.example: The binomial nomenclature on the label was Panthera leo.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上的双名学名是 Panthera leo。
senses.why: The phrase can shift from the system to one product of the system, just as a language can mean a sentence in that language.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以从体系转指体系的一个产物，正如一种语言也可指该语言中的一个句子。

senses.title: The formal code governing names
senses.titleCN: 管辖名称的正式法规
senses.definition: the set of international rules that determine which two-part name is valid
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪个两段式名称有效的国际规则
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature forbids using the same species epithet for two different genera in one publication.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法规禁止在同一出版物中把同一个种加词用于两个不同的属。
senses.why: A naming system needs arbitration; the phrase absorbs the rulebook that settles priority and validity.
senses.whyCN: 命名体系需要仲裁；这个短语也吸收了解决优先权与有效性的那本法规。

senses.title: The Latin-form name on a specimen label
senses.titleCN: 标本标签上的拉丁形式学名
senses.definition: the two-part Latin name printed on a specimen or collection label
senses.definitionCN: 印在标本或藏品标签上的两段式拉丁名称
senses.example: The students copied the binomial nomenclature from the herbarium sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们从腊叶标本纸上抄下双名学名。
senses.why: In the herbarium the system becomes a line of ink on paper, and that line is what the phrase points to.
senses.whyCN: 在标本馆里，体系变成纸上的一行墨迹，而这一行正是短语所指的东西。

senses.title: The naming practice within taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分类学内部的命名实践
senses.definition: the naming practice that taxonomy performs after a specimen has been identified
senses.definitionCN: 分类学在标本被鉴定之后所执行的命名实践
senses.example: Identification came first; binomial nomenclature followed once the genus was settled.
senses.exampleCN: 先鉴定，属确定之后才进行双名命名。
senses.why: Taxonomy has an order: decide what the thing is, then apply the two-part name according to the code.
senses.whyCN: 分类学有先后：先判断这是什么东西，再按法规给出两段式名称。

senses.title: A standard topic in biology teaching
senses.titleCN: 生物学教学中的标准课题
senses.definition: the curricular topic in which students learn to write and read two-part names
senses.definitionCN: 学生学习书写与认读两段式名称的课程主题
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature is taught alongside cell structure in the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法与细胞结构在第一学期同时讲授。
senses.why: A practice that every biologist must use becomes a lesson, and the phrase then names the lesson itself.
senses.whyCN: 每位生物学家都必须使用的做法会成为课程，短语于是也指这门课的内容。

senses.title: A two-part key in collection databases
senses.titleCN: 馆藏数据库中的两段式索引键
senses.definition: the two-part name field used to index specimens and records in a database
senses.definitionCN: 用于索引标本与记录的两段式名称字段
senses.example: The museum stores binomial nomenclature in a single searchable field.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把双名学名存放在一个可检索字段中。
senses.why: Digital collections turn the name into a key, so the phrase also labels the indexing convention.
senses.whyCN: 数字馆藏把名称变成索引键，短语于是也标记这种编目约定。

senses.title: A historical reform of biological naming
senses.titleCN: 生物学命名史上的一次改革
senses.definition: the historical shift from long descriptions to stable two-part names
senses.definitionCN: 从冗长描述转向稳定两段式名称的历史转变
senses.example: Binomial nomenclature made earlier polynomial names obsolete.
senses.exampleCN: 双名命名法使更早的多词名称被淘汰。
senses.why: Before the reform a species could carry a whole sentence of description; the phrase names the reform that ended that.
senses.whyCN: 改革之前，一个物种可能带着一整句描述；这个短语指的就是终结那种做法的改革。

intro.en: Binomial nomenclature joins a Late Latin adjective meaning having two names to a Latin noun meaning a calling of names; the phrase itself is a modern English combination, not a Latin formula.
intro.cn: binomial nomenclature 把晚期拉丁形容词「有两个名字的」与拉丁名词「呼名、名称清单」合在一起；短语本身是现代英语的组合，并非拉丁语原句。

items.en: Binomius, from bini two each and nomen name, described something carrying two names.
items.cn: binomius 由 bini「各两个」与 nomen「名字」构成，描述携带两个名字的事物。

items.en: Nomenclatura, from nomen and calator caller, meant the calling of names and then a list of names.
items.cn: nomenclatura 由 nomen 与 calator「呼名者」构成，先指呼名动作，后指名称清单。

items.en: Linnaeus made the two-part name standard in the eighteenth century, although he did not use the English phrase now attached to it.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪使两段式名称成为标准，尽管他本人并未使用今天附着其上的这个英语短语。

items.en: The English phrase binomial nomenclature spread in the nineteenth century as biology became a taught science with international codes.
items.cn: 随着生物学成为有国际法规的讲授学科，英语短语 binomial nomenclature 在 19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Modern botanical and zoological codes still regulate the phrase's practice, deciding priority, validity and permissible changes.
items.cn: 现代植物学与动物学法规仍管辖这一实践，决定优先权、有效性与允许的更改。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (FIRST DATE AND PHRASE ORIGIN)
items.en: Source uncertain as to the exact first use of the English phrase and the person who coined it; the component roots are clear, but the date is usually given only approximately, and no single originator is documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与短语来源）：英语短语的确切首用与首创者均无定论；各构词成分的词根清楚，但年代通常只给约数，也没有确凿的创制者。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that look similar but name different levels of classification; group two holds neighbouring terms in the vocabulary of biological naming.
note.cn: 第一组是形式相似但指不同分类层级的短语；第二组是生物命名词汇中相邻的术语。

entries.definition: The two-part name produced by the system; it is the product, while binomial nomenclature is the practice or system.
entries.definitionCN: 由该体系产出的两段式名称；它是产物，而 binomial nomenclature 指做法或体系。

entries.definition: The algebraic rewriting of a two-term expression; it shares the adjective but belongs to mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 对含两个项的表达式作代数展开；共享形容词，但属于数学。

entries.definition: Any formal name used in science; only the biological two-part kind falls under binomial nomenclature.
entries.definitionCN: 科学中使用的任何正式名称；只有生物学的两段式名称属于双名命名法。

entries.definition: The ordinary local name of an organism, which is not governed by binomial nomenclature at all.
entries.definitionCN: 生物在日常地方上的俗称，完全不受双名命名法管辖。

entries.definition: The whole science of grouping organisms, within which binomial nomenclature is the naming step.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物分组的整门科学，双名命名法是其中的命名步骤。

entries.definition: Any system of names; the phrase narrows this general word to the biological two-part case.
entries.definitionCN: 任何命名体系；这个短语把该泛称收窄到生物学的两段式情形。

entries.definition: A level such as genus or species; binomial nomenclature uses two of these ranks in one name.
entries.definitionCN: 属、种之类的层级；双名命名法在一个名称中使用其中两个层级。

entries.definition: The physical specimen that anchors a name; the name is binomial nomenclature, the anchor is the type.
entries.definitionCN: 为一个名称提供依据的实物标本；名称属双名命名法，依据则是模式标本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Binomial gives two parts, nomenclature gives the system: two-part naming as a practice.
normal.cn: binomial 给出两部分，nomenclature 给出体系：作为做法的两段式命名。

normal.en: The two parts are genus and species, always written in that order.
normal.cn: 两部分是属名与种名，永远按这个顺序书写。

normal.en: Linnaeus is the name attached to the reform, even though he did not coin the English phrase.
normal.cn: 林奈是与这场改革相连的名字，尽管英语短语并非他创制。

normal.en: International codes decide priority, so the phrase has a legal flavour.
normal.cn: 国际法规决定优先权，因此这个短语带有法律色彩。

normal.en: Herbarium sheets, museum labels and database fields all display the same two-part key.
normal.cn: 腊叶标本纸、博物馆标签与数据库字段都展示同一个两段式索引键。

abstract.en: Picture a plant wearing a two-word nametag at a conference.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物在会议上戴着两个词的胸牌。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every book has a shelf mark and a title joined as one code.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每本书的架号与书名合成一个编码。

abstract.en: Picture a law that begins before the trial and decides what the case may be called.
abstract.cn: 想象一部在审判之前就生效、决定案件可以如何命名的法律。

examples.en: Binomial nomenclature requires italics for the genus and species in print.
examples.cn: 双名命名法要求在印刷时把属名与种名排成斜体。

examples.en: Without binomial nomenclature, a species could carry a phrase as long as a sentence.
examples.cn: 没有双名命名法，一个物种可能带着像句子一样长的名称。

examples.en: The course began with binomial nomenclature and ended with phylogenetics.
examples.cn: 这门课从双名命名法开始，以系统发生学结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bi 两 + nomen 名字 + calare 呼叫」——用两个名字呼叫每个物种 → 双名命名法

root: 现代英语短语 = 晚期拉丁 binomius「有两个名字的」+ 拉丁 nomenclatura「呼名；名称清单」；两部分词根均清楚，短语首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a system to its product, its rulebook, its ink on a label, its place in taxonomy, its classroom form, its database key and its history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从体系走向产物、法规、标签上的墨迹、分类学中的位置、课堂形态、数据库索引键，最后走向历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one specimen, one card, two Latin words that together identify the species.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件标本、一张卡片、两个拉丁词合起来识别这个物种。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PRODUCT: the practice and the name it produces are two faces of the same phrase.
branches.cn: 体系与产物：做法与它产出的名称是同一短语的两面。

branches.en: CODE: international rules decide which two-part name is valid.
branches.cn: 法规：国际规则决定哪个两段式名称有效。

branches.en: VISIBLE KEY: on paper or in a database, the name becomes a searchable line.
branches.cn: 可见索引：无论在纸上还是数据库里，名称都变成可检索的一行。

branches.en: ORDER OF WORK: identify first, name second, and teach the practice to the next generation.
branches.cn: 工作次序：先鉴定，再命名，并把做法教给下一代。

branches.en: REFORM: the phrase also remembers the change from long descriptions to stable names.
branches.cn: 改革：短语还记住了从冗长描述到稳定名称的转变。

intro.en: The phrase is made of two learned Latin borrowings; pulling them apart shows how biology assembled a modern term from old parts.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个学术拉丁借词构成；把它们拆开，就能看出生物学如何用旧部件组装出一个现代术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin binomius supplies the two-part adjective; Latin nomenclatura supplies the system noun, built on nomen and calator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 binomius 提供「两部分」的形容词；拉丁 nomenclatura 提供「体系」名词，由 nomen 与 calator 构成。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数量固定为二。

items.example: Nomen is the root behind both halves of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: nomen 是短语两部分的共同词根。

items.example: The adjective entered English as binomial.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 binomial 进入英语。

items.example: The calling of names is the literal sense.
items.exampleCN: 「把名字叫出来」正是其字面义。

items.meaning: a calling of names; a list of names
items.exampleCN: nomenclatura 变成英语 nomenclature。
双名有两个部分。
命名体系遵循一部法规。
命名规则被引用了。

items.example: The binomial name was written in italics.
items.exampleCN: 双名学名用斜体书写。

latinEntries.meaning: a calling of names; a list

definition_zh: 形态学的；形态上的；词法上的；与结构形式有关的
definition_en: relating to form or structure, especially the form of organisms or of words
core_image: 同一物种的两副骨架并排摆放，形状的差别一眼可见，功能却尚未被测
scene: 在比较解剖实验室里，研究员把两块头骨并排摆开说：The morphological differences between the two skulls were obvious at a glance.
sceneCN: 这里 morphological 指「与形态结构有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及生物外形与结构的）；句意是两块头骨之间的形态差异一眼就能看出。

senses.title: Relating to the form of organisms
senses.titleCN: 与生物外形和结构有关的
senses.definition: relating to the outward form and structure of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 与生物的外形与结构有关的
senses.example: The morphological differences between the two skulls were obvious at a glance.
senses.exampleCN: 两块头骨之间的形态差异一眼就能看出。
senses.why: Morphē is Greek for form, so the adjective simply points to shape and structure rather than to behaviour or chemistry.
senses.whyCN: morphē 是希腊语「形状」，因此这个形容词指向形状与结构，而非行为或化学成分。

senses.title: Relating to the structure of words
senses.titleCN: 与词的内部结构有关的
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure and formation of words
senses.definitionCN: 与词的内部结构与构成有关的
senses.example: Morphological analysis splits running into a stem and a suffix.
senses.exampleCN: 形态分析把“running（跑）”拆成词干与后缀。
senses.why: Linguistics applied the same Greek word for form to the shape of words, where prefixes and suffixes are the visible parts.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把同一个表示「形状」的希腊词用在词的外形上，前缀与后缀就是可见的部件。

senses.title: Form as opposed to function
senses.titleCN: 与功能相对的形态层面
senses.definition: concerning shape or structure rather than purpose or function
senses.definitionCN: 关注形状或结构，而非用途或功能
senses.example: A morphological study describes the wing without asking how it works in flight.
senses.exampleCN: 形态研究描述翅膀的形状，而不追问它在飞行中如何起作用。
senses.why: Anatomy separates two questions: what a part looks like and what it does; morphological marks the first.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把两个问题分开：某部分长什么样、它做什么；morphological 标记的是前者。

senses.title: Relating to landforms
senses.titleCN: 与地貌形态有关的
senses.definition: relating to the shape of landforms and their development
senses.definitionCN: 与地貌的形状及其发育有关的
senses.example: The team mapped morphological features along the river terrace.
senses.exampleCN: 团队绘制了河流阶地上的地貌形态特征。
senses.why: Geology borrowed the form word for the surface shapes of the earth, which are read as evidence of past processes.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用了这个「形状」词来指地表的形态，这些形态被当作过去过程的证据来读。

senses.title: Relating to microstructure in materials
senses.titleCN: 与材料微观组织有关的
senses.definition: relating to the internal microstructure of a material
senses.definitionCN: 与材料内部微观组织有关的
senses.example: The alloy passed every morphological inspection before testing.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金在测试前通过了所有显微组织检查。
senses.why: Materials science extends form downward to grains and phases visible only under a microscope.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把「形状」向下延伸到只有显微镜下才可见的晶粒与相。

senses.title: Relating to galaxy shape
senses.titleCN: 与星系形状有关的
senses.definition: relating to the classification of galaxies by their shape
senses.definitionCN: 与按形状对星系分类有关的
senses.example: The survey recorded morphological types from spiral to elliptical.
senses.exampleCN: 这项巡天记录了从旋涡到椭圆的各形态类型。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the adjective to objects so distant that only their shape can be measured.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把这个形容词用于如此遥远的天体，因为能测量的只有它们的形状。

senses.title: Relating to word formation
senses.titleCN: 与构词方式有关的
senses.definition: relating to the patterns by which new words are built
senses.definitionCN: 与构造新词的规律有关的
senses.example: The language shows rich morphological compounding.
senses.exampleCN: 这种语言显示出丰富的形态复合构词。
senses.why: In grammar the term covers how roots combine with affixes to make new words, the form side of word formation.
senses.whyCN: 在语法中，这个词涵盖词根与词缀如何组合成新词，即构词的「形式」一面。

senses.title: Relating to outward shape in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指与外形容态有关的
senses.definition: relating to outward shape or configuration in any field
senses.definitionCN: 在任何领域中与外形容态有关的
senses.example: The critic offered a morphological reading of the city plan rather than a social one.
senses.exampleCN: 这位评论者对城市规划作了形态解读，而不是社会解读。
senses.why: Once the word means form anywhere, it can describe the layout of a city, a sentence or an institution without leaving the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词泛指任何领域的「形式」，它就能描述城市、句子或机构的布局，而不离开核心义。

intro.en: Morphological joins Greek morphē form to the suffix -logical, which comes from logos word or account; the deeper origin of morphē itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: morphological 把希腊 morphē「形状」接上来自 logos「言说、论述」的后缀 -logical；morphē 本身的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Morphē meant form, shape or outward appearance; its earlier origin is not established, and proposals linking it to meros part remain hypotheses.
items.cn: morphē 意为形状、外形或外观；其更早来源未得到证明，把它与 meros「部分」相联系的提法仍属假说。

items.en: Logos meant word, account or reasoning, and the combining form -logia grew from it to name a field of study.
items.cn: logos 意为言词、叙述或推理，组合形式 -logia 由此发展为指一门研究领域。

items.en: Modern Latin morphologia combined morphē with -logia, first for the study of form in biology and later in language.
items.cn: 近代拉丁 morphologia 把 morphē 与 -logia 组合起来，最初指生物学中的形态研究，后来也用于语言。

items.en: English morphology and morphological entered through German and French work in the nineteenth century, when biology and linguistics both needed a science of form.
items.cn: 英语的 morphology 与 morphological 经 19 世纪德语与法语著作进入，当时生物学与语言学都需要一门关于形式的科学。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the origin of Greek morphē is unresolved, so any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate, while the -logical suffix is well understood.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑、年代为约数）：希腊 morphē 的来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数，而 -logical 后缀的构成是清楚的。

note.en: Group one holds shape-related words that look alike but diverge in root or scope; group two holds near neighbours in the vocabulary of form and structure.
note.cn: 第一组是形似而词根或范围不同的「形状」类词；第二组是形式与结构词汇中意思相近的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the study or the form itself; morphological is simply its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究或形态本身的名词；morphological 只是它的形容词。

entries.definition: From morphē plus -eme: the smallest meaningful unit of a word, a specific linguistic application of form.
entries.definitionCN: morphē 加 -eme：词的最小意义单位，是「形式」在语言学中的具体应用。

entries.definition: A- without plus morphē: lacking a definite shape, which shows the same root in a negative compound.
entries.definitionCN: a-「无」加 morphē：没有确定形状，显示同一词根用于否定复合词。

entries.definition: Meta- across plus morphē: a complete change of form, as in an insect's life cycle.
entries.definitionCN: meta-「越过」加 morphē：形态的彻底改变，如昆虫的生活史。

entries.definition: Relating to the arrangement of parts, often with an emphasis on how the whole is put together rather than on visible shape.
entries.definitionCN: 与部件的排列有关，常强调整体如何组装，而不强调可见外形。

entries.definition: Relating to dissection and the parts of a body; it overlaps with morphological but is tied to internal organization.
entries.definitionCN: 与解剖和身体部件有关；与 morphological 有重叠，但更绑定内部组织。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to matter in general; it is broader and does not separate shape from function.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体或一般物质有关；范围更广，且不把形状与功能分开。

entries.definition: Relating to the observable traits produced by genes and environment; morphological traits are one subset of these.
entries.definitionCN: 与基因和环境共同产生的可观察性状有关；形态性状是其中一类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek morphē form plus -logical study: the adjective of the science of shape.
normal.cn: 希腊 morphē「形状」加 -logical「学科」：关于形状之学的形容词。

normal.en: The noun family runs morphology, morphologist, morphometrics.
normal.cn: 名词词族包括 morphology、morphologist、morphometrics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: morphological analysis, morphological change, morphological evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：形态分析、形态变化、形态学证据。

normal.en: Biology contrasts morphological with molecular evidence.
normal.cn: 生物学把形态学证据与分子证据相对照。

normal.en: Language uses the same adjective for word structure.
normal.cn: 语言学用同一个形容词指词的内部结构。

abstract.en: Picture two skeletons side by side while nobody asks what either of them did.
abstract.cn: 想象两副骨架并排摆着，却没人问它们各自做过什么。

abstract.en: Picture a word cut into pieces like a model kit.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词像模型套件那样被拆成几块。

abstract.en: Picture a river terrace seen from above as a pattern of lines.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看河流阶地，只见一片线条图案。

examples.en: Morphological evidence placed the fossil between two living groups.
examples.cn: 形态学证据把这块化石置于两个现存类群之间。

examples.en: The paper compares morphological and molecular data for the same species.
examples.cn: 这篇论文对同一物种比较了形态数据与分子数据。

examples.en: Children acquire morphological rules without explicit instruction.
examples.cn: 儿童无需明确教学就能习得构词规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「morph 形状 + logical 学理」——关于形状与结构的 → 形态学的、形态上的

root: 希腊 morphē「形状」+ -logical（出自 logos「言说、论述」）；morphē 的更深来源不确定，与 meros『部分』的联系仅为假说。英语经近代拉丁 morphologia 于 19 世纪进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to many kinds of shape: an organism, a word, a landform, a metal grain, a galaxy, a compound, a city plan and the contrast with function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于多种「形状」：生物、词、地貌、金属晶粒、星系、复合词、城市规划，以及与功能相对的层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two forms placed side by side so that the difference in shape can be seen before any question about use is asked.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种形态并排摆放，在追问用途之前先看出形状的差别。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL FORM: the adjective separates what a part looks like from what it does.
branches.cn: 生物形态：这个形容词把某部分长什么样与它做什么分开。

branches.en: WORD FORM: roots and affixes give words their internal shape.
branches.cn: 词的形式：词根与词缀给词以内部形状。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND LAND FORM: the same word reaches down to grains and out to river terraces.
branches.cn: 材料与地貌：同一个词向下到晶粒，向外到河流阶地。

branches.en: GALAXY SHAPE: at cosmic distance, shape is the only trait left to measure.
branches.cn: 星系形状：在宇宙尺度上，形状是唯一还能测量的性状。

branches.en: ANY CONFIGURATION: once form is abstract, a city plan can be read morphologically too.
branches.cn: 任何构形：一旦「形式」抽象化，城市规划也可作形态解读。

intro.en: Morphological is a Greek root plus a Greek-derived suffix, and the same two pieces build a large family of English technical words.
intro.cn: morphological 是一个希腊词根加一个希腊来源的后缀，这两个部件构成了一大批英语技术词。

latinIntro.en: Greek morphē supplies the form root; logos supplies -logia and -logical, which name fields of study from biology to linguistics.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 morphē 提供「形状」词根；logos 提供 -logia 与 -logical，用来命名从生物学到语言学的各个研究领域。

items.example: The root names shape in many technical words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在许多技术词中指形状。

items.example: The suffix turns a subject into a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一门主题变成研究领域。

items.example: Morphology describes the form of organisms.
items.exampleCN: 形态学描述生物的形态。

items.meaningCN: 与形态或形态学有关的
items.exampleCN: 形态差异很明显。
这两种贝壳在形态上不同。
一位形态学家测量了每件标本。

items.meaning: smallest meaningful unit of a word
items.example: The suffix is a separate morpheme.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀是一个独立的语素。

items.example: The sample was an amorphous solid.
items.exampleCN: 这个样品是无定形固体。
这种昆虫经历完全变态。

definition_zh: 形态学；形态；词法；地貌形态；组织结构
definition_en: the study of the form and structure of organisms, words, or other systems
core_image: 一张工作台上并排摆着骨骼、词卡与地形图，三样东西都在讲同一个问题：它们是什么形状
scene: 在大学的分类学课堂上，教授写下三个问题后说：Morphology alone cannot tell us how two species behave.
sceneCN: 这里 morphology 指「对生物形态的研究」（第 1 个义项：研究生物外形与结构的学科）；句意是单靠形态学无法告诉我们两个物种如何活动。

senses.title: The biological study of form
senses.titleCN: 研究生物形态的学科
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies the form and structure of organisms
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物外形与结构的生物学分支
senses.example: Morphology alone cannot tell us how two species behave.
senses.exampleCN: 单靠形态学无法告诉我们两个物种如何活动。
senses.why: Morphē is form and -logia is study, so the noun names a discipline before it names any particular shape.
senses.whyCN: morphē 是「形状」，-logia 是「研究」，因此这个名词先指一门学科，而非某个具体形状。

senses.title: The form itself, apart from its study
senses.titleCN: 形态本身（而非对其研究）
senses.definition: the actual form and structure of an organism or object
senses.definitionCN: 生物或物体的实际外形与结构
senses.example: The morphology of the shell suggests a burrowing animal.
senses.exampleCN: 贝壳的形态提示这是一种穴居动物。
senses.why: The same noun can metonymically name the object of study, so morphology means the shape as well as the science of shape.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以用转喻指研究对象，因此 morphology 既指学科，也指形状本身。

senses.title: The study of word structure
senses.titleCN: 研究词的内部结构的学问
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that studies how words are built from morphemes
senses.definitionCN: 研究词如何由语素构成的语言学分支
senses.example: English morphology explains why the plural ending changes shape.
senses.exampleCN: 英语词法解释了复数词尾为何改变形式。
senses.why: Linguists took the Greek form word for the internal shape of words, the arrangement of roots and affixes.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用了这个希腊「形状」词，指词的内部形状，即词根与词缀的排列。

senses.title: The shape of landforms
senses.titleCN: 地貌的形态
senses.definition: the form and development of landforms, studied in geomorphology
senses.definitionCN: 地貌的形状与发育，在地貌学中研究
senses.example: The morphology of the valley records repeated glacial advances.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷的形态记录了多次冰川推进。
senses.why: Earth science borrowed the word for the surface shapes of the planet, which are read as a history of process.
senses.whyCN: 地球科学借用这个词指地表的形状，这些形状被当作过程史来读。

senses.title: The shape of a galaxy
senses.titleCN: 星系的形态
senses.definition: the structural classification of galaxies by their shape
senses.definitionCN: 按形状对星系所作的结构分类
senses.example: Galaxy morphology divides spirals, ellipticals and irregulars.
senses.exampleCN: 星系形态学把星系分为旋涡、椭圆与不规则三类。
senses.why: At great distance only shape survives as evidence, so astronomy makes morphology a classification tool.
senses.whyCN: 在极远的距离上，只有形状还能作为证据，因此天文学把形态学当作分类工具。

senses.title: Microstructure of a material
senses.titleCN: 材料的微观组织
senses.definition: the internal structure of a material, such as grains and phases
senses.definitionCN: 材料的内部结构，如晶粒与相
senses.example: Heat treatment changed the morphology of the alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 热处理改变了这种合金的组织形态。
senses.why: Materials science applies the word to structures seen under a microscope, where shape controls strength.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把这个词用于显微镜下所见的结构，那里的形状决定强度。

senses.title: Mathematical morphology
senses.titleCN: 数学形态学
senses.definition: a branch of image analysis that studies shapes with set operations
senses.definitionCN: 用集合运算研究形状的图像分析分支
senses.example: Mathematical morphology removes noise by shrinking and expanding shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 数学形态学通过收缩与扩张形状来去除噪声。
senses.why: Here morphology is literal again: algorithms act on the shape of regions in an image.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 morphology 又回到字面义：算法作用于图像中区域的形状。

senses.title: The form of a city or institution
senses.titleCN: 城市或机构的形态
senses.definition: the spatial or organizational form of a settlement or system
senses.definitionCN: 聚落或系统的空间或组织形态
senses.example: Urban morphology maps streets, plots and building types together.
senses.exampleCN: 城市形态学把街道、地块与建筑类型放在一起绘制。
senses.why: Once form is the object, any organized layout can have a morphology, from streets to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「形式」成为对象，任何有组织的布局都可以有形态，从街道到机构。

intro.en: Morphology is Greek morphē form plus -logia study, mediated by modern Latin morphologia; the origin of morphē itself is unresolved.
intro.cn: morphology 是希腊 morphē「形状」加 -logia「研究」，经近代拉丁 morphologia 中介；morphē 本身的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Morphē meant form or outward appearance; its deeper origin is uncertain, and a link to meros part is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: morphē 意为形状或外观；其更深来源不确定，与 meros「部分」的联系只是假说。

items.en: Logia, from logos word or account, named a field of study when attached to a root.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos「言词、论述」，接在词根后便指一门研究领域。

items.en: Modern Latin morphologia assembled the two Greek pieces for the study of biological form.
items.cn: 近代拉丁 morphologia 把两个希腊部件组装起来，指对生物形态的研究。

items.en: Nineteenth-century German and French biologists and linguists established morphology as a named science in both fields.
items.cn: 19 世纪德国与法国的生物学家和语言学家使 morphology 在这两个领域都成为有名称的学科。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: Greek morphē has no established pre-Greek origin, so any reconstructed Indo-European base is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：希腊 morphē 没有已证实的希腊语之前来源，凡给出的印欧语基形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same form root; group two holds neighbouring disciplines that also describe structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「形状」词根构成的词；第二组是同样描述结构的相邻学科。

entries.definition: The adjective of morphology, used when a noun is needed for a trait or feature.
entries.definitionCN: morphology 的形容词，用于修饰性状或特征。

entries.definition: The smallest meaningful unit of a word; it is what morphology studies, not the study itself.
entries.definitionCN: 词的最小意义单位；它是形态学研究的对象，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: Without definite form, built from the same morphē root with a negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 没有确定形状，由同一 morphē 词根加否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: A complete change of form; the root is shared, but the meaning is transformation rather than study.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变；共享词根，但意义是转变而非研究。

entries.definition: The study of body parts by dissection; it overlaps with morphology but stresses internal organization.
entries.definitionCN: 通过解剖研究身体各部分的学问；与形态学重叠，但强调内部组织。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work; it is the functional counterpart of morphology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体各部位如何运作的学问；是形态学的功能对应面。

entries.definition: The science of grouping and naming organisms; morphology supplies much of its evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物分组与命名的科学；形态学为其提供大量证据。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts; morphology is the systematic study of that arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 部件的排列；形态学是对这种排列的系统研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Morphē form plus -logia study: the study of shape wherever shape matters.
normal.cn: morphē「形状」加 -logia「研究」：在形状重要的地方研究形状。

normal.en: The family runs morphology, morphological, morphologically, morphologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 morphology、morphological、morphologically、morphologist。

normal.en: The same noun covers organisms, words and cities.
normal.cn: 同一个名词覆盖生物、词与城市。

normal.en: Biology pairs morphology with physiology: form beside function.
normal.cn: 生物学把形态学与生理学配对：形式与功能并列。

normal.en: Galaxy morphology is a classification, not a laboratory study.
normal.cn: 星系形态学是一种分类，而非实验室研究。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench holding a bone, a word card and a map, all answering one question about shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，上面放着骨头、词卡和地图，都在回答同一个关于形状的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a city seen from above as a sentence written in streets.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城市，街道写成了一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a metal grain enlarged until its outline becomes a landscape.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒金属被放大，轮廓变成一片地貌。

examples.en: Her research combines morphology with molecular phylogeny.
examples.cn: 她的研究把形态学与分子系统发生学结合起来。

examples.en: The morphology of the leaf separates the two varieties.
examples.cn: 叶片的形态把这两个变种区分开来。

examples.en: Urban morphology studies how plots and streets evolve together.
examples.cn: 城市形态学研究地块与街道如何一起演变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「morph 形状 + ology 学科」——研究形状与结构的学问 → 形态学、词法

root: 希腊 morphē「形状」+ -logia「研究」（出自 logos「言说、论述」），经近代拉丁 morphologia；morphē 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show one discipline spreading across organisms, words, landforms, galaxies, materials, images and cities, while the core question stays the same: what is the shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项显示同一门学问铺展到生物、词、地貌、星系、材料、图像与城市，而核心问题始终不变：形状是什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench where a bone, a word card and a map are examined for the same property, their shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工作台上放着骨头、词卡与地图，被检查的是同一个属性——形状。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND OBJECT: morphology is both the study of form and the form being studied.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：形态学既是研究形式的学问，也是被研究的形式本身。

branches.en: WORD SHAPE: roots and affixes are the anatomy of a word.
branches.cn: 词的形状：词根与词缀就是词的解剖结构。

branches.en: LAND AND SKY: the same word describes river terraces and spiral galaxies.
branches.cn: 大地与天空：同一个词描述河流阶地与旋涡星系。

branches.en: MICRO AND ALGORITHM: grains under a microscope and shapes inside an image are read the same way.
branches.cn: 微观与算法：显微镜下的晶粒与图像里的形状用同一种方式读取。

branches.en: ORGANIZED SPACE: a city or an institution can be studied as a form.
branches.cn: 有组织的空间：城市或机构可以作为形式来研究。

intro.en: Morphology is a two-part Greek compound, and each part recurs in a large technical vocabulary shared by biology, linguistics and medicine.
intro.cn: morphology 是一个两部分希腊复合词，每个部分都重现于生物学、语言学与医学共用的技术词汇中。

latinIntro.en: Greek morphē gives the form root; Greek logos gives -logia, the suffix of disciplines from biology to sociology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 morphē 给出「形状」词根；希腊 logos 给出 -logia，即从生物学到社会学的学科后缀。

items.example: The root names shape across many fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在多个领域指形状。
这个后缀命名一门学科。

items.example: Morphology describes the form of organisms.
items.exampleCN: 形态学描述生物的形态。
形态数据支持这一划分。
形态学家测量了贝壳。
每个词尾都是一个语素。
玻璃是无定形的。
幼虫经历变态。
地貌学解释了这条山谷。

definition_zh: 形态变异；形态差异；（生物或词形）外形与结构上的变异
definition_en: differences in form and structure among organisms, populations, or word forms
core_image: 同一片山坡上的同种甲虫，鞘翅长短不一，排成一列像一把参差的尺
scene: 在山坡样方里，研究员量完一排甲虫后说：Morphological variation within this population is wider than we expected.
sceneCN: 这里 morphological variation 指「同一物种内部个体之间外形与结构的差异」（第 1 个义项：种群内的形态变异）；句意是这个种群内部的形态变异比我们预想的更大。

senses.title: Shape differences within one species
senses.titleCN: 同一物种内部的形态差异
senses.definition: differences in form among individuals of the same species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种不同个体在外形与结构上的差异
senses.example: Morphological variation within this population is wider than we expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这个种群内部的形态变异比我们预想的更大。
senses.why: Morphological names the form and variation names the spread; together they say that members of one kind are not all built alike.
senses.whyCN: morphological 指形态，variation 指差异；合起来就是说同一类成员并非长得一模一样。

senses.title: Differences between separated populations
senses.titleCN: 分隔种群之间的形态差异
senses.definition: form differences among populations across a geographic range
senses.definitionCN: 分布区内不同种群之间的外形差异
senses.example: Geographic morphological variation follows the temperature gradient.
senses.exampleCN: 地理形态变异沿温度梯度变化。
senses.why: When populations are split by distance, their forms drift apart, and the phrase records that pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当种群被距离隔开，它们的外形会逐渐分化，这个短语记录的就是这种格局。

senses.title: Variation in word forms
senses.titleCN: 语言中词形的变异
senses.definition: differences in the shape of a word or morpheme across contexts or dialects
senses.definitionCN: 词或语素在不同语境或方言中形式上的差异
senses.example: Morphological variation in the plural ending reveals the language's history.
senses.exampleCN: 复数词尾的形态变异揭示了这种语言的历史。
senses.why: Linguistics reuses the same phrase for the changing shape of words rather than of bodies.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把这个短语移用于词形而非身体形状的变化。

senses.title: Shape differences across life stages
senses.titleCN: 不同发育阶段的形态差异
senses.definition: form differences between developmental stages of one organism
senses.definitionCN: 同一生物在不同发育阶段之间的外形差异
senses.example: Morphological variation between the larva and the adult is extreme.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫与成体之间的形态差异极大。
senses.why: A single organism can wear very different forms in one lifetime, so variation is measured across time as well as across individuals.
senses.whyCN: 同一个生物一生中可以呈现很不同的形态，因此变异既跨个体也跨时间测量。

senses.title: Shape differences in the fossil record
senses.titleCN: 化石记录中的形态变异
senses.definition: form differences observed among fossils of the same or related species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种或近缘物种化石之间观察到的外形差异
senses.example: Morphological variation in the fossil teeth suggested several diets.
senses.exampleCN: 化石牙齿的形态变异提示存在多种食性。
senses.why: When only bones remain, shape is the main evidence, and its spread becomes a clue to past diversity.
senses.whyCN: 当只剩骨骼时，形状是主要证据，形状的离散程度就成为过去多样性的线索。

senses.title: Measured variation in shape traits
senses.titleCN: 对形态性状所作的测量变异
senses.definition: statistically measured differences in shape traits within a sample
senses.definitionCN: 样本内形态性状差异的统计测量
senses.example: The team quantified morphological variation with landmark measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用标志点测量量化了形态变异。
senses.why: Once variation is measured, the phrase belongs to statistics: it names the spread of shape values, not a vague impression.
senses.whyCN: 一旦变异被测量，这个短语就属于统计学：它指形状数值的离散程度，而非模糊印象。

senses.title: Shape differences caused by environment
senses.titleCN: 由环境引起的形态差异
senses.definition: form differences produced by environmental conditions acting on the same genotype
senses.definitionCN: 相同基因型在不同环境条件下产生的形态差异
senses.example: Morphological variation across the slope came from differences in water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 坡面各处的形态变异来自供水差异。
senses.why: The same genetic instructions can build different bodies under different conditions, so the phrase also covers environmentally induced spread.
senses.whyCN: 同一套遗传指令在不同条件下可以造出不同的身体，因此这个短语也涵盖环境诱发的差异。

senses.title: Variation in plant reproductive structures
senses.titleCN: 植物生殖结构上的形态变异
senses.definition: form differences in flowers, seeds or other reproductive parts
senses.definitionCN: 花、种子或其他生殖部位在形态上的差异
senses.example: Morphological variation in flower size affects which insects visit.
senses.exampleCN: 花大小的形态变异会影响哪些昆虫来访。
senses.why: In botany the phrase often points at reproductive parts, because their shape decides how pollen travels.
senses.whyCN: 在植物学中，这个短语常指向生殖部位，因为它们的形状决定花粉如何传播。

intro.en: Morphological variation joins a Greek-derived adjective about form to a Latin-derived noun about difference; the phrase is a modern technical combination rather than an inherited unit.
intro.cn: morphological variation 把源自希腊语的「形态」形容词与源自拉丁语的「差异」名词合在一起；这是现代技术短语，而非承袭下来的固定单位。

items.en: Morphē meant form or shape; its deeper origin is uncertain, and links to meros part remain hypotheses.
items.cn: morphē 意为形状或外形；其更深来源不确定，与 meros「部分」的联系仍属假说。

items.en: Variare meant to change or make different, from varius varied or mottled; the deeper origin of varius is not established.
items.cn: variare 意为改变、使不同，来自 varius「多变的、斑驳的」；varius 的更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: VARIATIO meant a changing or difference, and English variation descends from it through French.
items.cn: variatio 意为变化或差异，英语 variation 经法语承袭自它。

items.en: Morphological entered English in the nineteenth century and variation much earlier; their combination belongs to modern biology and linguistics.
items.cn: morphological 在 19 世纪进入英语，variation 进入更早；两者的组合属于现代生物学与语言学。

items.en: The phrase spread with studies of populations, fossils and dialects, where measuring difference in form became routine.
items.cn: 随着种群、化石与方言研究的发展，这个短语传播开来，测量形态差异成为常规工作。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (PHRASE DATE AND VARIUS ROOT)
items.en: Source uncertain in two respects: the first use of the English phrase is not fixed, and the root of Latin varius is unresolved, so any Indo-European base offered for it is a reconstruction; the morphē root is clear in shape but uncertain in deeper origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定有两处：英语短语的首见无法确定；拉丁 varius 的词根尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语基形式均属重构形式；morphē 的词形清楚，但更深来源不确定。

note.en: Group one holds the component words and their near forms, which are often swapped by mistake; group two holds technical neighbours that measure difference differently.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混用的组成部分及其近形词；第二组是以不同方式衡量差异的技术近邻词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing form; alone it says nothing about difference, which variation adds.
entries.definitionCN: 描述形态的形容词；单独使用时不表示差异，差异由 variation 承担。

entries.definition: The study of form; the phrase names a phenomenon studied, not the study itself.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形态的学科；短语命名的是被研究的现象，而非学科。

entries.definition: Difference or change in general; without morphological it could refer to price, temperature or pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指差异或变化；没有 morphological 时也可指价格、温度或音高。

entries.definition: A single form that differs from others; variation is the spread among many such forms.
entries.definitionCN: 一个与其他形式不同的单个形式；variation 是许多此类形式之间的整体差异。

entries.definition: Differences in observable traits, of which morphological variation is the shape-based part.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察性状上的差异，形态变异是其中以形状为基础的部分。

entries.definition: Differences in genes among individuals; it may or may not show up as morphological variation.
entries.definitionCN: 个体之间基因上的差异；它可能表现为形态变异，也可能不表现。

entries.definition: The existence of several clearly distinct forms in one population, a coarse-grained case of morphological variation.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种群中存在几种明显不同的形态，是形态变异的粗粒情形。

entries.definition: One genotype producing different forms under different conditions, the mechanism behind one kind of morphological variation.
entries.definitionCN: 同一基因型在不同条件下产生不同形态，是某一类形态变异背后的机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Morphological about form, variation about spread: the spread of shapes.
normal.cn: morphological 管形态，variation 管离散：形状的离散程度。

normal.en: The phrase is standard in population biology, paleontology and dialectology.
normal.cn: 这个短语在种群生物学、古生物学与方言学中都是标准说法。

normal.en: Measure it with landmarks, ratios or counts of teeth.
normal.cn: 可用标志点、比例或牙齿计数来测量它。

normal.en: Contrast it with genetic variation: genes underneath, shapes on the surface.
normal.cn: 与遗传变异对照：基因在下，形状在上。

normal.en: Flower size and leaf shape are classic examples.
normal.cn: 花的大小与叶的形状是经典例子。

abstract.en: Picture a row of beetles whose wing cases form a jagged ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一排甲虫，鞘翅排成一把参差的尺。

abstract.en: Picture one song sung in many accents across a valley.
abstract.cn: 想象同一首歌在山谷各处用不同口音唱出。

abstract.en: Picture the same clay pressed by different thumbs.
abstract.cn: 想象同一团泥被不同的拇指按出不同形状。

examples.en: The researchers mapped morphological variation along an altitude gradient.
examples.cn: 研究者沿海拔梯度绘制了形态变异。

examples.en: Morphological variation in the wings distinguishes the two subspecies.
examples.cn: 翅膀上的形态变异把这两个亚种区分开来。

examples.en: The study separates environmental from genetic sources of morphological variation.
examples.cn: 这项研究把形态变异的环境来源与遗传来源分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「morph 形状 + logical 学理 + variation 差异」——形状上的差异 → 形态变异

root: morphological = 希腊 morphē「形状」+ -logical；variation = 拉丁 variare「改变」，出自 varius「多变的」（更深来源不确定）。短语为现代技术组合，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track one idea through scales: one population, separated populations, words, life stages, fossils, measured traits, environments and flowers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个观念追过不同尺度：单个种群、分隔种群、词、发育阶段、化石、测量性状、环境与花。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind of body, repeated many times, never twice identical.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一种身体被重复许多次，却从不完全相同。

branches.en: SPREAD IN SPACE: one species, many places, forms drifting apart.
branches.cn: 空间离散：一个物种分布多处，形态逐渐分开。

branches.en: WORD FORM: the same mechanism appears in the endings of words.
branches.cn: 词形：同一机制出现在词的词尾上。

branches.en: SPREAD IN TIME: life stages and fossils show form changing across ages.
branches.cn: 时间离散：发育阶段与化石显示形态跨越时代而变化。

branches.en: MEASURE AND CAUSE: shape values are counted, and environment is one cause of their spread.
branches.cn: 测量与成因：形状数值被计数，环境是离散的成因之一。

branches.en: REPRODUCTIVE FORM: flower shape decides which visitors carry pollen.
branches.cn: 生殖形态：花的形状决定哪种来访者携带花粉。

intro.en: The phrase is a transparent compound of a Greek-derived adjective and a Latin-derived noun, and each half has its own productive family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个希腊来源的形容词与一个拉丁来源的名词透明组合而成，每一半都有自己的能产词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek morphē builds morphology and morphological; Latin varius and variare build variation, variant and various.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 morphē 构成 morphology 与 morphological；拉丁 varius 与 variare 构成 variation、variant 与 various。

items.example: The root names shape in many technical words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在许多技术词中表示形状。

items.example: The suffix turns morphology into its adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 morphology 变成形容词。

items.example: The verb underlies variation and vary.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 variation 与 vary 的基础。
variatio 变成英语 variation。
形态性状被记录下来。
变异以毫米为单位测量。

items.structure: variant-, present participle stem of variare
items.example: A rare variant appeared in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 样本中出现一个罕见变体。
发现了多种形状。
形态学提供方法。

definition_zh: 生理学；生理机能；（某生物或某系统的）生理特性
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies how living systems function, or the functions themselves
core_image: 一间实验室里，跑步机连着呼吸面罩，屏幕上跳动的曲线记录身体在运动时如何耗氧
scene: 运动生理实验室里，研究员看着屏幕说：Physiology explains why the runner's heart rate climbs so quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 physiology 指「研究生命系统如何运作的生理学」（第 1 个义项：研究身体机能的学科）；句意是生理学解释了这位跑者心率为何升得这么快。

senses.title: The science of how living systems work
senses.titleCN: 研究生命系统如何运作的学科
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies the functions of living organisms and their parts
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体及其各部位功能的生物学分支
senses.example: Physiology explains why the runner's heart rate climbs so quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 生理学解释了这位跑者心率为何升得这么快。
senses.why: Physis is nature and -logia is study; the word began as an inquiry into nature and narrowed to the functions of living bodies.
senses.whyCN: physis 是「自然」，-logia 是「研究」；这个词最初指对自然的探究，后来收窄为对生命体机能的探究。

senses.title: The functions themselves
senses.titleCN: 生理机能本身
senses.definition: the actual functioning of a living organism or system
senses.definitionCN: 生命体或系统实际的运作方式
senses.example: The physiology of the diving seal conserves oxygen for long periods.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水海豹的生理机能可长时间保存氧气。
senses.why: Like morphology, the noun can name the object of study rather than the study, so physiology also means the functioning itself.
senses.whyCN: 与 morphology 一样，这个名词也可指研究对象而非学科，因此 physiology 也指运作本身。

senses.title: The functional traits of one organism
senses.titleCN: 某一生物特有的生理特性
senses.definition: the particular functional characteristics of a given species or individual
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或个体特有的功能特征
senses.example: The physiology of this cactus suits a desert with rare rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仙人掌的生理特性适应少雨的沙漠。
senses.why: The word narrows from the general science to the specific set of functions that makes one organism suited to its life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从普通学科收窄为某一生物适应其生活的一套具体机能。

senses.title: Plant physiology as a branch
senses.titleCN: 作为分支的植物生理学
senses.definition: the study of how plants take up water, make food and respond to their environment
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物如何吸水、制造养分并回应环境的分支
senses.example: Plant physiology studies how roots sense drought before leaves wilt.
senses.exampleCN: 植物生理学研究根如何在叶片萎蔫之前察觉干旱。
senses.why: Each kingdom gets its own physiology, because plants solve the same problems with different machinery.
senses.whyCN: 每个生物界都有自己的生理学，因为植物用不同机制解决同样的问题。

senses.title: Exercise physiology as a branch
senses.titleCN: 作为分支的运动生理学
senses.definition: the study of how the body responds and adapts to physical activity
senses.definitionCN: 研究身体如何回应并适应体育活动的分支
senses.example: Exercise physiology measures oxygen uptake during a sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 运动生理学测量短跑时的摄氧量。
senses.why: When muscles are pushed, the functions become measurable, and a whole applied branch grows around that setting.
senses.whyCN: 当肌肉受到推动时，机能变得可测量，一整个应用分支便围绕这一情境生长出来。

senses.title: Cell physiology
senses.titleCN: 细胞生理学
senses.definition: the study of the functions of cells and their membranes
senses.definitionCN: 研究细胞及其膜功能的学问
senses.example: Cell physiology asks how ions cross a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞生理学追问离子如何穿过细胞膜。
senses.why: The same word scales down to the cell, where function means transport, signalling and metabolism.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词可缩小到细胞尺度，那里的功能指运输、信号与代谢。

senses.title: Comparative physiology
senses.titleCN: 比较生理学
senses.definition: the study of functional differences across species
senses.definitionCN: 研究不同物种之间功能差异的学问
senses.example: Comparative physiology shows how the same organ works at different temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 比较生理学显示同一器官在不同温度下如何运作。
senses.why: Comparing functions across species turns physiology into an evolutionary tool as well as a medical one.
senses.whyCN: 跨物种比较功能，使生理学既是医学工具，也是演化工具。

senses.title: The functioning of one body system
senses.titleCN: 某一身体系统的运作
senses.definition: the functional behaviour of a particular organ or system
senses.definitionCN: 某一器官或系统的功能表现
senses.example: Cardiac physiology covers the filling and pumping of the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏生理学涵盖心脏的充盈与泵血。
senses.why: Any organ can be given its own physiology, since each has a set of jobs that can be described on its own.
senses.whyCN: 任何器官都可以有自己的生理学，因为每个器官都有一组可单独描述的工作。

intro.en: Physiology comes from Latin physiologia, from Greek physiologia, an inquiry into nature, built on physis nature and -logia study; the modern medical sense is later and narrower.
intro.cn: physiology 来自拉丁 physiologia，再上溯希腊 physiologia「对自然的探究」，由 physis「自然」与 -logia「研究」构成；现代医学义更晚、更窄。

items.en: Physis meant nature or the essential character of a thing; it derives from phyein to grow, and the deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: physis 意为自然或事物的本性；它来自 phyein「生长」，更深的印欧语形式属重构形式。

items.en: Phyein meant to bring forth, grow or spring up; the idea of growth underlies the word for nature.
items.cn: phyein 意为产生、生长、萌发；生长的观念构成「自然」一词的基础。

items.en: Logia, from logos, named the study or account of a subject.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos，指对某主题的研究或论述。

items.en: Latin took the Greek compound as physiologia, still meaning inquiry into nature rather than medicine.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这一希腊复合词作 physiologia，仍指对自然的探究，而非医学。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the late sixteenth century; the narrower sense of bodily functions became dominant in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪晚期借入该词；到 19 世纪，指身体机能的较窄义成为主导。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (DATE APPROXIMATE, DEEP ROOT RECONSTRUCTED)
items.en: Source uncertain only in detail: the first English date is approximate, and any Indo-European base for phyein is a reconstruction; the Greek compound itself is well attested.
items.cn: 来源仅在细节上不确定：英语首见年代为约数，phyein 的任何印欧语基形式均属重构；希腊复合词本身有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Greek nature root that are often confused with physiology; group two holds neighbouring life-science disciplines.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「自然」词根、常与 physiology 混淆的词；第二组是相邻的生命科学学科。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to body functions; it describes a trait, while physiology names the field or the functions.
entries.definitionCN: 表示与身体机能有关的形容词；它描述性状，而 physiology 指学科或机能本身。

entries.definition: A person who studies physiology; the -ist suffix turns the field into its practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生理学的人；-ist 后缀把学科变成从业者。

entries.definition: The form and build of a body, from the same Greek nature root but focusing on shape rather than function.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形貌与体格，同出希腊「自然」词根，但侧重形状而非功能。

entries.definition: The science of matter and energy, from Greek physika natural things; it shares the root but studies non-living systems.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学，来自希腊 physika「自然之物」；共享词根，但研究非生命系统。

entries.definition: The study of life in general; physiology is one of its branches.
entries.definitionCN: 对生命的一般研究；生理学是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: The study of body structure; it supplies the parts that physiology explains the workings of.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体结构的学问；它提供部件，生理学解释这些部件如何运作。

entries.definition: The job a part performs; physiology is the systematic study of such jobs.
entries.definitionCN: 某部件所执行的工作；生理学是对这些工作的系统研究。

entries.definition: The chemistry of living systems; it explains many mechanisms that physiology describes at the body level.
entries.definitionCN: 生命系统的化学；它解释许多生理学在身体层面描述的机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Physis nature plus -logia study: the study of how living nature works.
normal.cn: physis「自然」加 -logia「研究」：研究活的自然如何运作。

normal.en: The family runs physiology, physiological, physiologist, physiologically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 physiology、physiological、physiologist、physiologically。

normal.en: Exercise, plant, comparative and cardiac physiology are fixed branches.
normal.cn: 运动、植物、比较与心脏生理学是固定分支。

normal.en: Anatomy gives the parts; physiology gives the workings.
normal.cn: 解剖学给出部件；生理学给出运作方式。

normal.en: The word narrowed from all of nature to living bodies.
normal.cn: 这个词从整个自然收窄到生命体。

abstract.en: Picture a dashboard of dials, each recording one body process.
abstract.cn: 想象一块仪表盘，每个表盘记录一项身体过程。

abstract.en: Picture a city's utility maps showing water, power and waste at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市的管线图，同时显示水、电与废物。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose manual explains only what each part does, never what it is made of.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器的手册只解释每个部件做什么，从不讲它由什么构成。

examples.en: She teaches physiology to first-year medical students.
examples.cn: 她给一年级医学生讲授生理学。

examples.en: The physiology of high-altitude birds has been studied for decades.
examples.cn: 高原鸟类的生理学已被研究数十年。

examples.en: His paper links physiology with behaviour in ants.
examples.cn: 他的论文把蚂蚁的生理与行为联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「physio 自然/身体 + ology 学科」——研究身体如何运作 → 生理学

root: 拉丁 physiologia，出自希腊 physiologia「对自然的探究」= physis「自然」（来自 phyein「生长」）+ -logia「研究」；更深印欧语基为重构形式，英语首见年代约 16 世纪晚期。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole science to the functions it studies, then to one organism, one branch, one setting, one cell and one organ.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整门学科走向它所研究的机能，再走向单个生物、单个分支、单个情境、单个细胞与单个器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body on a treadmill, wired to dials that turn invisible workings into visible curves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体在跑步机上接着仪表，把看不见的运作变成可见的曲线。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND OBJECT: physiology is both the study of function and the function studied.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：生理学既是研究机能的学问，也是被研究的机能。

branches.en: ONE ORGANISM: a species carries its own set of working arrangements.
branches.cn: 单个生物：每个物种带着自己的一套运作安排。

branches.en: APPLIED BRANCHES: plants and athletes pose different functional questions.
branches.cn: 应用分支：植物与运动员提出不同的功能问题。

branches.en: SCALES: the same word covers a cell membrane and a whole heart.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一个词覆盖细胞膜与整颗心脏。

branches.en: COMPARISON: putting species side by side turns function into evidence for evolution.
branches.cn: 比较：把物种并排摆开，功能便成为演化证据。

intro.en: Physiology is a Greek compound whose parts recur in medicine and biology, so the word can be read as nature plus study.
intro.cn: physiology 是一个希腊复合词，其部件在医学与生物学中反复出现，因此可按「自然 + 研究」读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek physis and phyein give physics, physique and physiology; Greek logos gives -logia and the names of disciplines.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 physis 与 phyein 衍生 physics、physique 与 physiology；希腊 logos 衍生 -logia 及学科名称。

items.example: The root survives in physics and physiology.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根存留于 physics 与 physiology 中。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of growth inside nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为「自然」注入生长的观念。

items.example: The suffix names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门研究领域。

items.example: Latin borrowed the word unchanged in sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语原样借入这个词，意义未变。
生理学解释了心率。
生理反应被记录下来。
生理学家测量了摄氧量。

items.meaning: the science of matter and energy
items.exampleCN: 物理学研究非生命物质。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful physique.
items.exampleCN: 这名运动员体格强壮。

definition_zh: 生理的；生理学的；由身体机能引起的
definition_en: relating to the functions of living bodies or to physiology as a science
core_image: 体检报告上一排数值：心率、体温、血氧，每个数字都在说身体正在做什么
scene: 在医院检查室里，医生看完报告说：The patient's symptoms are physiological, not psychological.
sceneCN: 这里 physiological 指「由身体机能引起的」（第 3 个义项：源于生理过程而非心理因素）；句意是这位病人的症状属于生理性的，而非心理性的。

pos.zh: 生理性的；由身体机能引起的

senses.title: Relating to body functions
senses.titleCN: 与身体机能有关的
senses.definition: relating to the normal functions of a living body
senses.definitionCN: 与生命体正常机能有关的
senses.example: The drug lowers blood pressure through a physiological route.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药通过生理途径降低血压。
senses.why: Physiology names the functions, and -ical makes the adjective: whatever touches those functions is physiological.
senses.whyCN: physiology 指机能，-ical 构成形容词：凡涉及这些机能的即为 physiological。

senses.title: Relating to physiology as a science
senses.titleCN: 与生理学这门学科有关的
senses.definition: belonging to the science of physiology or its methods
senses.definitionCN: 属于生理学这门学科或其方法的
senses.example: The paper reports physiological measurements taken in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文报告了实验室中取得的生理学测量结果。
senses.why: The adjective can point at the discipline rather than the body, marking methods, data or literature.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可指向学科而非身体，标记方法、数据或文献。

senses.title: Caused by bodily processes
senses.titleCN: 由身体过程引起的
