senses.definition: produced by bodily processes rather than by psychological or external causes
senses.definitionCN: 由身体过程而非心理或外部原因造成的
senses.example: The patient's symptoms are physiological, not psychological.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人的症状属于生理性的，而非心理性的。
senses.why: The word draws a line: whatever arises from the body's workings is physiological, as opposed to mental.
senses.whyCN: 这个词划出一条界线：凡源自身体运作的即为生理性，与心理性相对。

senses.title: Normal rather than pathological
senses.titleCN: 正常生理性的而非病理性的
senses.definition: belonging to normal healthy functioning rather than to disease
senses.definitionCN: 属于正常健康机能而非疾病的
senses.example: The swelling is physiological and will fade without treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这种肿胀是生理性的，不经治疗也会消退。
senses.why: A second contrast appears here: physiological means the body doing what it normally does, not a disorder.
senses.whyCN: 这里出现第二种对照：生理性指身体按正常方式运作，而非病变。

senses.title: Relating to plant functions
senses.titleCN: 与植物生理功能有关的
senses.definition: relating to the functions of plants
senses.definitionCN: 与植物的生理功能有关的
senses.example: Physiological drought can strike even when the soil is wet.
senses.exampleCN: 即使土壤湿润，也可能发生生理性干旱。
senses.why: Plants have functions too, so the same adjective covers water transport and photosynthesis.
senses.whyCN: 植物也有机能，因此同一个形容词也涵盖水分运输与光合作用。

senses.title: At the level of cells and tissues
senses.titleCN: 细胞与组织层面的生理的
senses.definition: relating to functions at the cellular or tissue level
senses.definitionCN: 与细胞或组织层面的功能有关的
senses.example: Physiological conditions in the tissue favoured repair.
senses.exampleCN: 组织内的生理条件有利于修复。
senses.why: The body's workings can be described at a smaller scale, where the adjective marks the local environment.
senses.whyCN: 身体的运作可在更小尺度上描述，这个形容词标记的正是局部环境。

senses.title: Relating to basic bodily needs
senses.titleCN: 与基本生理需求有关的
senses.definition: relating to needs such as food, water, warmth and rest
senses.definitionCN: 与食物、水、温暖与休息等需求有关的
senses.example: The shelter first meets physiological needs before offering counselling.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所先满足生理需求，再提供咨询。
senses.why: Needs that the body itself generates are called physiological, a usage made familiar by psychology.
senses.whyCN: 由身体本身产生的需求被称为生理需求，这一用法因心理学而广为人知。

senses.title: A bodily response studied in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中研究的身体反应
senses.definition: a bodily reaction measured in psychological experiments
senses.definitionCN: 心理学实验中测量的身体反应
senses.example: Physiological responses such as sweating were recorded during the test.
senses.exampleCN: 测试过程中记录了出汗等生理反应。
senses.why: Psychology measures the body to read the mind, so the adjective often appears in studies of emotion.
senses.whyCN: 心理学通过测量身体来读取心理，因此这个形容词常出现在情绪研究中。

intro.en: Physiological is physiology plus the adjective suffix -ical, so it inherits the Greek roots physis nature and logos study; the adjective itself is a modern formation.
intro.cn: physiological 是 physiology 加形容词后缀 -ical，因此承袭希腊词根 physis「自然」与 logos「研究」；这个形容词本身是近代构词。

items.en: Physis meant nature, from phyein to grow; the deeper Indo-European base is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: physis 意为自然，来自 phyein「生长」；更深的印欧语基属重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Physiologia combined physis with -logia to name an inquiry into nature.
items.cn: physiologia 把 physis 与 -logia 组合起来，指对自然的探究。

items.en: Latin physiologia passed into English as physiology, and the adjective was built on it with -ical.
items.cn: 拉丁 physiologia 以 physiology 进入英语，形容词再由它加 -ical 构成。

items.en: As laboratory medicine grew, physiological became the standard word for processes of the healthy body.
items.cn: 随着实验室医学发展，physiological 成为指健康身体过程的标准词。

items.en: Psychology later adopted the adjective for bodily responses and for basic needs, adding two applied senses.
items.cn: 心理学后来采用这个形容词指身体反应与基本需求，增添了两个应用义项。

items.en: Source uncertain only in detail: the first date of the English adjective is approximate, and the Indo-European base of phyein is a reconstruction; the Greek and Latin lineage is well attested.
items.cn: 来源仅在细节上不确定：英语形容词的首见年代为约数，phyein 的印欧语基属重构形式；希腊语与拉丁语的承袭线有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Greek nature root but name different things; group two holds words close in meaning when describing the body.
note.cn: 第一组是共享希腊「自然」词根但所指不同的词；第二组是描述身体时意思相近的词。

entries.definition: Relating to matter or the body as an object; it does not specifically mean the body's workings, which physiological does.
entries.definitionCN: 与物质或作为对象的身体有关；它不特指身体的运作，而 physiological 特指运作。

entries.definition: The shape and build of a body; it names appearance rather than function.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形状与体格；它指外观而非功能。

entries.definition: A medical doctor; the word once meant a student of natural philosophy, but now names a person, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 医生；这个词曾指自然哲学的学习者，如今指人而非过程。

entries.definition: The science of matter and energy; it shares the root but studies non-living systems.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学；共享词根，但研究非生命系统。

entries.definition: Relating to life or living things broadly; physiological is narrower and points at functions.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛指与生命或生物有关；physiological 更窄，指向功能。

entries.definition: A plainer word for what belongs to the body; it lacks the scientific focus on function.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于身体的较通俗词；缺少对功能的科学侧重。

entries.definition: Relating to the body, especially non-reproductive cells; it is a technical near-synonym in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关，尤指非生殖细胞；医学中是技术性近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to how something works or whether it works; physiological is the body-specific version.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物如何运作或是否运作有关；physiological 是身体专用的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Physiology plus -ical: the adjective of body function.
normal.cn: physiology 加 -ical：身体机能的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs physiology, physiologist, physiologically, physiopathology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 physiology、physiologist、physiologically、physiopathology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: physiological response, needs, process, adaptation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：生理反应、生理需求、生理过程、生理适应。

normal.en: The key contrast is physiological versus psychological.
normal.cn: 关键对照是生理性与心理性。

normal.en: Another contrast is physiological versus pathological.
normal.cn: 另一组对照是生理性与病理性。

abstract.en: Picture a dashboard where every dial reports a body process.
abstract.cn: 想象一块仪表盘，每个表盘都报告一项身体过程。

abstract.en: Picture two doors, one marked body and one marked mind.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，一扇标着身体，一扇标着心理。

abstract.en: Picture a plant quietly opening and closing its pores.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物安静地开合它的气孔。

examples.en: Sleep fulfils a physiological need that no schedule can remove.
examples.cn: 睡眠满足一种任何日程都无法取消的生理需求。

examples.en: The study measured physiological stress during the examination.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了考试期间的生理应激。

examples.en: Physiological research often begins with a simple blood sample.
examples.cn: 生理学研究常从一份简单的血样开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「physio 身体 + logical 学理」——关于身体运作的 → 生理的、生理学的

root: physiology + -ical；physiology 出自拉丁 physiologia，源自希腊 physis「自然」（来自 phyein「生长」）+ -logia「研究」；形容词首见年代为约数，phyein 印欧语基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the adjective to functions, the discipline, bodily causes, normal health, plants, cells, basic needs and psychological measurement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词用于机能、学科、身体成因、正常健康、植物、细胞、基本需求与心理测量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of readings on a medical report, each number reporting what the body is doing.
core.cn: 核心意象：体检报告上一排读数，每个数字都报告身体正在做什么。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND FIELD: the adjective covers both the body's workings and the science that studies them.
branches.cn: 机能与学科：这个形容词同时覆盖身体运作与研究它的学问。

branches.en: BODY VERSUS MIND: a symptom is called physiological when its cause lies in the body.
branches.cn: 身体对心理：当成因在身体时，症状被称为生理性的。

branches.en: NORMAL VERSUS DISEASED: physiological also means healthy functioning rather than pathology.
branches.cn: 正常对病变：physiological 也指健康运作而非病理。

branches.en: SCALES OF LIFE: plants and cells have functions that the same adjective describes.
branches.cn: 生命尺度：植物与细胞也有同一形容词可描述的功能。

branches.en: NEED AND MEASUREMENT: psychology borrowed the word for basic needs and for bodily responses.
branches.cn: 需求与测量：心理学借这个词指基本需求与身体反应。

intro.en: Physiological is a compound of a Greek-derived noun and a Latin-derived suffix, and the whole family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: physiological 由一个希腊来源的名词与一个拉丁来源的后缀构成，整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek physis gives physics and physiology; Latin -icus, through French -ique and English -ical, supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 physis 给出 physics 与 physiology；拉丁 -icus 经法语 -ique 与英语 -ical 提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The root survives in physics and physiology.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根存留于 physics 与 physiology 中。
physiologia 变成英语 physiology。

items.example: Physiology studies how the heart pumps.
items.exampleCN: 生理学研究心脏如何泵血。

items.example: The suffix turns nouns into adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。
生理反应被记录下来。
这两种状态在生理上不同。
生理学家主持了这项试验。
物理学研究非生命物质。

items.example: The swimmer has a strong physique.
items.exampleCN: 这位游泳者体格强壮。

definition_zh: 生理学家；研究生理机能的人
definition_en: a scientist who studies the functions of living organisms
core_image: 一位穿白大褂的研究者站在跑步机旁，手里拿着记录本，眼睛盯着氧耗曲线
scene: 在高原研究站里，项目负责人介绍团队时说：The physiologist will measure how our bodies adapt to low oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 physiologist 指「研究生命体机能的科学家」（第 1 个义项：从事生理学研究的人）；句意是这位生理学家将测量我们的身体如何适应低氧。

pos.zh: 生理学家；生理学研究者

senses.title: A scientist of body functions
senses.titleCN: 研究身体机能的科学家
senses.definition: a scientist whose field is the functions of living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 以生命体机能为研究领域的科学家
senses.example: The physiologist will measure how our bodies adapt to low oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家将测量我们的身体如何适应低氧。
senses.why: Physiology names the field and -ist names the person, so the word is simply the practitioner of that science.
senses.whyCN: physiology 指学科，-ist 指人，因此这个词就是该科学的从业者。

senses.title: A medical physiologist
senses.titleCN: 医学生理学家
senses.definition: a specialist who studies body functions in relation to health and disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究与健康和疾病相关的身体机能的专家
senses.example: The medical physiologist traced the hormone's effect on kidney function.
senses.exampleCN: 这位医学生理学家追踪了该激素对肾功能的影响。
senses.why: Medicine narrows the field to the functions that keep people well or make them ill.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这一领域收窄到维持健康或导致疾病的机能。

senses.title: A plant physiologist
senses.titleCN: 植物生理学家
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how plants function
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物如何运作的科学家
senses.example: The plant physiologist grafted shoots to test water uptake.
senses.exampleCN: 这位植物生理学家嫁接枝条以检验吸水情况。
senses.why: Plants pose different functional problems, so the same title takes a botanical specialism.
senses.whyCN: 植物提出不同的功能问题，因此同一头衔可带植物学专长。

senses.title: An exercise physiologist
senses.titleCN: 运动生理学家
senses.definition: a specialist in how the body responds to exercise
senses.definitionCN: 研究身体如何回应运动的专家
senses.example: The exercise physiologist designed a training plan around oxygen capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 这位运动生理学家围绕摄氧能力设计了训练计划。
senses.why: Sport turns function into performance, and a whole applied role grows around the measurement.
senses.whyCN: 运动把机能变成表现，一整个应用角色便围绕测量生长出来。

senses.title: A comparative physiologist
senses.titleCN: 比较生理学家
senses.definition: a scientist who compares functions across species
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较机能的科学家
senses.example: The comparative physiologist compared heat loss in desert and arctic mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位比较生理学家比较了沙漠与北极哺乳动物的散热。
senses.why: Comparison across species makes the physiologist an evolutionary as well as a laboratory worker.
senses.whyCN: 跨物种比较使生理学家既是实验室工作者，也是演化研究者。

senses.title: A laboratory researcher
senses.titleCN: 实验室里的研究者
senses.definition: a researcher who runs controlled experiments on living systems
senses.definitionCN: 对生命系统进行受控实验的研究者
senses.example: The physiologist recorded breathing rates for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家记录了六小时的呼吸频率。
senses.why: The title also marks a working role: someone who instruments, records and repeats measurements.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔也标记一种工作角色：安装仪器、记录并重复测量的人。

senses.title: A teacher of physiology
senses.titleCN: 生理学教师
senses.definition: a person who teaches physiology to students
senses.definitionCN: 向学生讲授生理学的人
senses.example: The physiologist lectured on circulation before the practical class.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家在实验课之前讲了循环系统。
senses.why: A researcher who teaches carries the same title, because the field and the classroom share one name.
senses.whyCN: 做研究又教学的人带着同一头衔，因为研究与课堂共享一个学科名。

senses.title: An author or expert consulted
senses.titleCN: 被咨询的生理学专家或作者
senses.definition: a recognized expert whose written or spoken judgement is sought
senses.definitionCN: 其书面或口头判断被求教的公认专家
senses.example: The physiologist was asked to review the safety data.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家被请去审查安全数据。
senses.why: Outside the lab the title works as credentials, allowing others to rely on a judgement they cannot make themselves.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室之外，这个头衔是一种资历，使他人能依赖自己无法作出的判断。

intro.en: Physiologist is physiology plus the agent suffix -ist, which reached English through Latin and French from Greek -istēs; the whole word is a nineteenth-century formation.
intro.cn: physiologist 是 physiology 加施事后缀 -ist，该后缀经拉丁语与法语来自希腊 -istēs；整词是 19 世纪的构词。

items.en: Physis meant nature, from phyein to grow; the deeper Indo-European base is reconstructed.
items.cn: physis 意为自然，来自 phyein「生长」；更深的印欧语基属重构形式。

items.en: Physiologia joined physis to -logia, naming an inquiry into nature.
items.cn: physiologia 把 physis 与 -logia 结合，指对自然的探究。

items.en: The agent suffix -istēs marked a person who does or practises something, and it became Latin -ista and English -ist.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -istēs 标记从事或实践某活动的人，后变为拉丁 -ista 与英语 -ist。

items.en: English physiology arrived in the late sixteenth century; the personal noun followed once the field had a professional identity.
items.cn: 英语 physiology 于 16 世纪晚期进入；待该领域形成职业身份后，指人的名词随之出现。

items.en: As laboratories and medical schools expanded, physiologist separated from physician and biologist as a distinct title.
items.cn: 随着实验室与医学院扩张，physiologist 与 physician、biologist 分离，成为独立头衔。

items.en: Source uncertain only as to the first date of the English personal noun, which is usually given approximately; the roots and the suffix are well attested.
items.cn: 来源仅在人称名词的英语首见年代上不确定，通常只给约数；词根与后缀均有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds titles and words that look almost identical to physiologist; group two holds neighbouring scientific roles.
note.cn: 第一组是几乎与 physiologist 同形的头衔与词；第二组是相邻的科学职业。

entries.definition: The science itself; the -ist form names the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 这门科学本身；-ist 形式指从事它的人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing functions; it modifies nouns but does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述机能的形容词；它修饰名词，但不指人。

entries.definition: A medical doctor; the ending looks similar but the word names a clinician, not a researcher in physiology.
entries.definitionCN: 医生；词尾看似相近，但这个词指临床医生，而非生理学研究者。

entries.definition: A specialist in physics; one letter apart in speech, a different science entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 物理学专家；语音上只差一点，却是完全不同的学科。

entries.definition: A scientist of life broadly; physiology is one of the biologist's possible specialisms.
entries.definitionCN: 广义研究生命的科学家；生理学是生物学家可能选择的专长之一。

entries.definition: A specialist in body structure; the anatomist describes parts, the physiologist explains their workings.
entries.definitionCN: 身体结构的专家；解剖学家描述部件，生理学家解释其运作。

entries.definition: A scientist of the chemistry of life; much physiological work is done at this molecular level.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生命化学的科学家；许多生理学工作在这一分子层面完成。

entries.definition: A doctor who treats patients; a physiologist may advise clinicians without treating anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 诊治病人的医生；生理学家可能为临床医生提供建议，却不亲自治疗。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Physiology plus -ist: the person who practises the science of function.
normal.cn: physiology 加 -ist：实践机能科学的人。

normal.en: The title takes specialisms: exercise, plant, clinical, comparative.
normal.cn: 这个头衔可带专长：运动、植物、临床、比较。

normal.en: The family runs physiology, physiological, physiologically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 physiology、physiological、physiologically。

normal.en: A physiologist measures; an anatomist describes; a clinician treats.
normal.cn: 生理学家测量，解剖学家描述，临床医生治疗。

normal.en: The person noun arose as laboratories created a profession.
normal.cn: 随着实验室造就一种职业，指人的名词才出现。

abstract.en: Picture a researcher standing beside a treadmill with a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象一位研究者拿着记录本站在跑步机旁。

abstract.en: Picture a translator who turns body signals into numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一位译者，把身体信号转成数字。

abstract.en: Picture a mechanic who studies engines without repairing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一位技师研究引擎却不修车。

examples.en: The physiologist spent the summer measuring oxygen use in migrant birds.
examples.cn: 这位生理学家整个夏天都在测量候鸟的耗氧量。

examples.en: A plant physiologist explained why the leaves closed at noon.
examples.cn: 一位植物生理学家解释了叶片为何在正午闭合。

examples.en: The committee invited a physiologist to assess the exercise protocol.
examples.cn: 委员会请了一位生理学家评估这套运动方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「physio 身体 + logist 研究者」——研究身体如何运作的人 → 生理学家

root: physiology + -ist（希腊 -istēs「从事者」）；physiology 源自希腊 physis「自然」+ -logia「研究」；整词为 19 世纪构词，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general scientist to medical, plant, exercise and comparative roles, then to the lab worker, the teacher and the consulted expert.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般科学家走向医学、植物、运动与比较角色，再走向实验室工作者、教师与被咨询的专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a notebook beside a body in motion, turning function into recorded numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着记录本站在运动中的身体旁，把机能变成记录下来的数字。

branches.en: FIELD AND PERSON: the title is simply the science plus the agent suffix.
branches.cn: 学科与人：头衔就是学科加施事后缀。

branches.en: SPECIALISM: plants and athletes turn the same title into different jobs.
branches.cn: 专长：植物与运动员使同一头衔变成不同工作。

branches.en: COMPARISON AND LAB: some compare species, others record one system for hours.
branches.cn: 比较与实验室：有人比较物种，有人连续数小时记录一个系统。

branches.en: TEACHING: the researcher also stands in front of a class.
branches.cn: 教学：研究者也站在课堂前面。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: outside the lab the title lets others trust a judgement.
branches.cn: 权威：在实验室之外，头衔使他人信任某种判断。

intro.en: Physiologist is a Greek-derived field name plus a Greek-derived agent suffix, and both parts are highly productive in English.
intro.cn: physiologist 是一个希腊来源的领域名加一个希腊来源的施事后缀，两部分在英语中都高度能产。

latinIntro.en: Greek physis gives physiology; Greek -istēs, through Latin -ista, gives the person suffix seen in biologist, chemist and economist.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 physis 给出 physiology；希腊 -istēs 经拉丁 -ista 给出 biologist、chemist、economist 中可见的指人后缀。

items.example: The root survives in physics and physiology.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根存留于 physics 与 physiology 中。
physiologia 变成 physiology。
生理学是这一领域。

items.example: The suffix turns a field into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把领域变成职业。
生理学家测量了摄氧量。
生理数据被收集。
这一反应在生理上不同。
生物学家在池塘取样。
解剖学家解剖了标本。

definition_zh: 发育；发展；开发；进展；（土地的）开发；显影；住宅小区；展开部
definition_en: the process of growing, changing or becoming more advanced, or a new event, product or built area that results
core_image: 一颗种子在窗台上依次裂开、抽芽、长叶，同一只花盆里装着好几个阶段
scene: 在育苗温室里，技术员指着不同高度的幼苗说：The development of these seedlings depends on light and temperature.
sceneCN: 这里 development 指「生物逐步生长发育的过程」（第 1 个义项：从幼体到成体的成长过程）；句意是这些幼苗的发育取决于光照与温度。

senses.title: Growth from an early stage
senses.titleCN: 从早期阶段逐步成长
senses.definition: the gradual growth of an organism or thing from a simpler to a more advanced state
senses.definitionCN: 生物或事物从较简单状态逐步成长为较高级状态
senses.example: The development of these seedlings depends on light and temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这些幼苗的发育取决于光照与温度。
senses.why: Develop began as unwrapping: something folded up is opened out step by step, and that is the shape of growth.
senses.whyCN: develop 最初意为「把包着的东西展开」：卷起之物被一步步打开，这正是成长的形状。

senses.title: Economic or social development
senses.titleCN: 经济或社会的发展
senses.definition: the improvement of a region's economy, institutions or living standards
senses.definitionCN: 某地区经济、制度或生活水平的改善
senses.example: Road access accelerated the region's economic development.
senses.exampleCN: 通路加速了该地区的经济发展。
senses.why: The same unfolding is applied to a whole society, where capacity is opened out over years.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「展开」被用于整个社会，能力在多年间被打开。

senses.title: Product or software development
senses.titleCN: 产品或软件的开发
senses.definition: the work of designing and building a new product or system
senses.definitionCN: 设计并构建新产品或系统的工作
senses.example: Product development took three cycles of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 产品开发经历了三轮测试。
senses.why: Here what unfolds is a design, from an idea to a working object that did not exist before.
senses.whyCN: 这里被展开的是设计，从想法变成此前不存在的可用物件。

senses.title: A new event or turn of events
senses.titleCN: 新事件或事态的新进展
senses.definition: a newly occurring event or change in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 新发生的事件或形势的新变化
senses.example: The latest development changed the terms of the negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 最新进展改变了谈判的条件。
senses.why: A happening can also be pictured as something unfolding, so the word names the next turn in a story.
senses.whyCN: 发生之事也可被想象为正在展开之物，因此这个词指故事中的下一个转折。

senses.title: Land development
senses.titleCN: 土地开发
senses.definition: the process of preparing land for building or use
senses.definitionCN: 把土地整理以备建造或使用的过程
senses.example: Land development destroyed part of the coastal marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 土地开发毁掉了部分滨海沼泽。
senses.why: Land is opened up for use, the original image made literal on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 土地被打开以供使用，最初的意象在地面上变成字面事实。

senses.title: Photographic development
senses.titleCN: 照片显影
senses.definition: the chemical process that makes a hidden image visible
senses.definitionCN: 使潜像变为可见影像的化学过程
senses.example: Careful development brought out the faint stars in the negative.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细显影使底片上微弱的星光显现出来。
senses.why: A latent image unfolds into a visible one, which is why photography borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 潜像展开为可见影像，摄影正是因此借用了这个词。

senses.title: A housing development
senses.titleCN: 新建的住宅小区
senses.definition: a group of new houses or buildings built as one project
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个项目建成的一组新住宅或建筑
senses.example: The development on the hill includes a school and a clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 山上的住宅小区包括一所学校和一间诊所。
senses.why: The product of land development takes the name of the process, so a place can be called a development.
senses.whyCN: 土地开发的产物沿用了过程之名，于是一处地方也可称为 development。

senses.title: The development section in music
senses.titleCN: 音乐中的展开部
senses.definition: the part of a musical work where themes are unfolded and transformed
senses.definitionCN: 音乐作品中把主题展开并变形处理的部分
senses.example: The development restates the opening theme in a new key.
senses.exampleCN: 展开部用新的调性重述开头的主题。
senses.why: Music kept the oldest sense: a theme is literally unfolded, turned over and recombined.
senses.whyCN: 音乐保留了最古老的义项：主题被字面地展开、翻转与重组。

intro.en: Development is develop plus -ment; develop came through French from Old French desveloper, to unwrap, whose second element is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: development 是 develop 加 -ment；develop 经法语来自古法语 desveloper「打开包裹」，其第二部分来源不确定。

items.en: Desveloper meant to unwrap, unfurl or uncover, built with des- un- and a second element voloper to wrap; the origin of voloper is not established.
items.cn: desveloper 意为打开包裹、展开、揭开，由 des-「去除」与表示「包裹」的 voloper 构成；voloper 的来源未得到证明。

items.en: The root of voloper is uncertain: a link to Latin volvere to roll has been proposed as a hypothesis, but it is not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: voloper 的词根不确定：有人提出它与拉丁 volvere「卷、滚」相关，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: French développer carried the sense of unfolding and gradually revealing, and English borrowed it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 développer 带有展开与逐步显露之义，英语于 17 世纪借入。

items.en: English develop first meant to unfold or bring out what was latent, including the working out of a musical theme.
items.cn: 英语 develop 最初指展开或使潜藏之物显现，包括把音乐主题铺展开来。

items.en: Industrial and urban growth added economic, product and housing senses, while photography added the image sense.
items.cn: 工业与城市增长增添了经济、产品与住宅义，摄影则增添了影像义。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the pre-French origin of voloper is unresolved, so any Latin or Germanic base offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate, while the -ment suffix is clear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑、年代为约数）：voloper 在法语之前的来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的拉丁或日耳曼语基形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数，而 -ment 后缀的构成清楚。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like development but contain a different wrapping root; group two holds near neighbours in the vocabulary of growth and change.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 development 却含不同「包裹」词根的词；第二组是成长与变化词汇中意思相近的词。

entries.definition: The verb underneath the noun: to unfold or bring out gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 名词底下的动词：展开或逐步带出。

entries.definition: Relating to development, especially the growth of organisms or children.
entries.definitionCN: 与发育有关的，尤指生物或儿童的成长。

entries.definition: From en- in plus the wrapping root: to cover or surround, the opposite direction of develop.
entries.definitionCN: 由 en-「进入」加「包裹」词根构成：覆盖或包围，与 develop 的方向相反。

entries.definition: The act of wrapping something round; it shares the wrapping element but not the sense of unfolding.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物包起来的行为；共享「包裹」成分，但没有「展开」之义。

entries.definition: An increase in size or amount; development can include growth but also change in quality and organization.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量的增加；development 可含增长，也含质量与组织的变化。

entries.definition: Movement toward a better or later state; development stresses unfolding, progress stresses advance.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好或更晚状态的移动；development 强调展开，progress 强调前进。

entries.definition: Slow, continuous change, often in populations or systems; development is usually the growth of one thing.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢连续的变化，常指种群或系统；development 通常指单个事物的成长。

entries.definition: An increase in extent or scope; development may involve expansion but also differentiation.
entries.definitionCN: 范围或规模的扩大；development 可包含扩张，也包含分化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Develop plus -ment: the process of unfolding something latent.
normal.cn: develop 加 -ment：把潜藏之物展开的过程。

normal.en: The family runs develop, developer, developmental, developmentally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 develop、developer、developmental、developmentally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: economic development, product development, land development.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：经济发展、产品开发、土地开发。

normal.en: Photography uses the word for making a hidden image visible.
normal.cn: 摄影用这个词指使潜像显影。

normal.en: Music uses it for the section where themes are unfolded.
normal.cn: 音乐用它指主题被展开的那一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a seed opening on a windowsill, one stage at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上一颗种子逐阶段打开。

abstract.en: Picture a folded map slowly spread across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起的地图在桌上慢慢展开。

abstract.en: Picture a negative turning into a sky full of stars.
abstract.cn: 想象一张底片变成满天星斗。

examples.en: The report links childhood development to clean water.
examples.cn: 这份报告把儿童发育与清洁饮水联系起来。

examples.en: The company increased its research and development budget.
examples.cn: 公司增加了研究与开发预算。

examples.en: A new development in the case forced a second hearing.
examples.cn: 案件的新进展促使第二次开庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de 去掉 + velop 包裹」——把包着的东西打开 → 展开、发育、发展

root: develop + -ment；develop 经法语来自古法语 desveloper「打开包裹」= des-「去除」+ voloper「包裹」（词根不确定，与拉丁 volvere 的联系仅为假说）。英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one metaphor: something folded or hidden is opened out, whether a seedling, an economy, a product, a plot of land, a latent image, a news story or a musical theme.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个比喻展开：折叠或隐藏之物被打开，无论是幼苗、经济、产品、地块、潜像、新闻事件还是音乐主题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed on a windowsill opening stage by stage in the same pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上同一只花盆里的种子逐阶段打开。

branches.en: GROWTH: an organism or a society opens out capacities over time.
branches.cn: 成长：生物或社会随时间展开其能力。

branches.en: BUILDING: a design is unfolded into a working product.
branches.cn: 建造：设计被展开为可用产品。

branches.en: EVENT: a situation unfolds into its next turn.
branches.cn: 事件：形势展开到下一个转折。

branches.en: LAND: ground is opened for use, and the result is also called a development.
branches.cn: 土地：土地被打开使用，其结果也被称为开发项目。

branches.en: REVELATION: a latent image or a musical theme is unfolded into view.
branches.cn: 显现：潜像或音乐主题被展开而可见。

intro.en: Development is a French-derived verb plus the Latin suffix -ment, and the family spreads across construction, photography and music.
intro.cn: development 是一个法语来源的动词加拉丁后缀 -ment，其词族铺展到建筑、摄影与音乐。

latinIntro.en: Old French desveloper supplies the verb; Latin -mentum, through French -ment, supplies the noun ending that names a result or process.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 desveloper 提供动词；拉丁 -mentum 经法语 -ment 提供指结果或过程的名词词尾。

items.example: The prefix turns wrapping into unwrapping.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包裹」变成「打开包裹」。
这个动词的来源不确定。

items.example: The bud developed into a leaf.
items.exampleCN: 芽展开成叶。

items.meaning: result or process of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: the process of unfolding or growth
items.exampleCN: 幼苗的发育需要光照。

items.meaning: a person or firm that develops
items.example: The developer built the new block.
items.exampleCN: 开发商建起了新街区。
发育阶段被比较。
这些儿童在发育上不同。
雾笼罩了山谷。

latinEntries.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 胚胎学；对胚胎及其发育的研究
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies embryos and their development
core_image: 一排玻璃皿里躺着从单细胞到成形幼体的序列，像一条把时间摊开来看的走廊
scene: 在发育生物学实验室里，教授指着培养箱说：Embryology traces how a single cell becomes a complex organism.
sceneCN: 这里 embryology 指「研究胚胎及其发育的学科」（第 1 个义项：胚胎学）；句意是胚胎学追踪单个细胞如何变成一个复杂的生物体。

senses.title: The science of embryos
senses.titleCN: 研究胚胎的学科
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies embryos and their development
senses.definitionCN: 研究胚胎及其发育的生物学分支
senses.example: Embryology traces how a single cell becomes a complex organism.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎学追踪单个细胞如何变成一个复杂的生物体。
senses.why: Embryon is the Greek word for a young one still growing, and -logia is study, so the noun names the discipline first.
senses.whyCN: embryon 是希腊语中指仍在生长的幼体，-logia 是研究，因此这个名词首先指学科。

senses.title: The development of an embryo
senses.titleCN: 胚胎的发育过程
senses.definition: the process by which an embryo forms and grows
senses.definitionCN: 胚胎形成与生长的过程
senses.example: The embryology of the frog was observed day by day.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙的胚胎发育被逐日观察。
senses.why: Like other -ology nouns, it can name the object of study, so embryology also means the development being studied.
senses.whyCN: 与其他 -ology 名词一样，它也可指研究对象，因此 embryology 也指被研究的发育过程。

senses.title: The embryological account of a species
senses.titleCN: 某一物种的胚胎发育叙述
senses.definition: the particular developmental history of a given species
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定物种的胚胎发育史
senses.example: The embryology of the sea urchin is unusually well documented.
senses.exampleCN: 海胆的胚胎发育记录得格外详尽。
senses.why: Narrowing from the science to one species gives a species-specific account of how its young form.
senses.whyCN: 从学科收窄到一个物种，就得到该物种幼体如何形成的专门叙述。

senses.title: Comparative embryology
senses.titleCN: 比较胚胎学
senses.definition: the comparison of embryonic development across species
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较胚胎发育的学问
senses.example: Comparative embryology once supplied key evidence for common descent.
senses.exampleCN: 比较胚胎学曾为共同祖先提供关键证据。
senses.why: Putting embryos of different animals side by side turns development into evolutionary evidence.
senses.whyCN: 把不同动物的胚胎并排摆放，就把发育变成演化证据。

senses.title: Medical embryology
senses.titleCN: 医学胚胎学
senses.definition: the study of human embryonic development for clinical purposes
senses.definitionCN: 为临床目的研究人类胚胎发育的学问
senses.example: Medical embryology explains the origin of certain heart defects.
senses.exampleCN: 医学胚胎学解释了某些心脏缺陷的成因。
senses.why: Clinicians need the embryonic timeline to understand which structures can go wrong and when.
senses.whyCN: 临床医生需要胚胎时间表，才能理解哪些结构会在何时出错。

senses.title: Plant embryology
senses.titleCN: 植物胚胎学
senses.definition: the study of embryos within seeds and their formation
senses.definitionCN: 研究种子内胚胎及其形成的学问
senses.example: Plant embryology begins with the fertilized egg inside the ovule.
senses.exampleCN: 植物胚胎学从胚珠内的受精卵开始。
senses.why: Plants keep their embryos inside seeds, so their embryology follows a different physical route.
senses.whyCN: 植物把胚胎留在种子里，因此其胚胎学走的是另一条物理路径。

senses.title: Embryological evidence for evolution
senses.titleCN: 支持演化的胚胎学证据
senses.definition: the use of shared embryonic features as evidence of relatedness
senses.definitionCN: 用共享的胚胎特征作为亲缘关系证据
senses.example: Embryology was cited long before genes could be compared.
senses.exampleCN: 在能够比较基因之前，胚胎学就已被援引。
senses.why: Similar embryos in different animals suggest a shared developmental programme inherited from a common ancestor.
senses.whyCN: 不同动物相似的胚胎提示一套从共同祖先继承来的发育程序。

senses.title: An academic course or textbook
senses.titleCN: 一门课程或一本教材
senses.definition: the taught subject or textbook treatment of embryonic development
senses.definitionCN: 作为教学科目或教材内容的胚胎发育
senses.example: Embryology is taught in the second year of the medical curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎学在医学课程的第二年讲授。
senses.why: A research field becomes a subject with lectures and chapters, and the same noun covers that classroom form.
senses.whyCN: 一个研究领域会成为有讲座与章节的科目，同一个名词也覆盖这种课堂形态。

intro.en: Embryology joins Greek embryon young one to -logia study; embryon itself is built from en- in and bryein to swell, and the deeper origin of bryein is uncertain.
intro.cn: embryology 把希腊 embryon「幼体」与 -logia「研究」结合；embryon 本身由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成，bryein 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one still forming, and also a swelling; the literal image is something growing inside.
items.cn: embryon 意为仍在形成的幼体，也指肿块；字面意象是某物在里面生长。

items.en: En- meant in, and bryein meant to swell or be full; the compound pictured life swelling inside a container.
items.cn: en- 意为「在内」，bryein 意为「膨胀、充满」；复合词描绘生命在容器内膨胀。

items.en: Logia, from logos, named the study or account of a subject.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos，指对某主题的研究或论述。

items.en: Modern Latin embryologia assembled embryon and -logia as a name for the study of embryonic development.
items.cn: 近代拉丁 embryologia 把 embryon 与 -logia 组装起来，作为研究胚胎发育的名称。

items.en: English embryology spread in the nineteenth century as comparative and experimental studies of development expanded.
items.cn: 随着发育的比较与实验研究扩张，英语 embryology 在 19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of Greek bryein is unresolved, so any Indo-European base offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（bryein 词根存疑、年代为约数）：希腊 bryein 的更深来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语基形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the embryo root that are often confused with the discipline name; group two holds neighbouring fields that also study development.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词根、常与学科名混淆的词；第二组是同样研究发育的相邻领域。

entries.definition: The developing organism itself; embryology is the study of it, not the thing studied.
entries.definitionCN: 正在发育的生物体本身；embryology 是对它的研究，而非被研究之物。

entries.definition: Relating to an embryo; it describes a structure or stage, while embryology names a field.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚胎有关的；它描述结构或阶段，而 embryology 指学科。

entries.definition: A person who studies embryos; the -ist form is the practitioner of embryology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的人；-ist 形式是 embryology 的从业者。

entries.definition: A biological variant of embryonic, used mainly in technical descriptions of embryonic tissue.
entries.definitionCN: embryonic 的生物学异体，主要用于描述胚胎组织的技术文本。

entries.definition: The broader study of how organisms grow; embryology is its classic embryo-focused core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物如何生长的更广领域；胚胎学是其以胚胎为核心的经典部分。

entries.definition: The study of developmental abnormalities; it shares embryology's timeline but focuses on defects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究发育异常的学问；共享胚胎学的时间线，但聚焦缺陷。

entries.definition: The study of body structure; embryology explains how that structure comes to exist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体结构的学问；胚胎学解释该结构如何形成。

entries.definition: The study of tissues; embryonic tissue is one of its early subjects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究组织的学问；胚胎组织是其早期研究对象之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Embryon young one plus -logia study: the study of the forming young.
normal.cn: embryon「幼体」加 -logia「研究」：研究正在形成的幼体。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryonic, embryology, embryologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryonic、embryology、embryologist。

normal.en: Comparative, experimental, medical and plant embryology are fixed branches.
normal.cn: 比较、实验、医学与植物胚胎学是固定分支。

normal.en: The field is tied to a timeline: fertilization, cleavage, gastrulation, organ formation.
normal.cn: 这门学科绑在一条时间线上：受精、卵裂、原肠形成、器官发生。

normal.en: Medical embryology explains birth defects by asking when a structure failed.
normal.cn: 医学胚胎学通过追问某结构何时出错来解释出生缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of glass dishes, each holding one moment of the same life.
abstract.cn: 想象一条玻璃皿走廊，每只皿装着同一生命的一个瞬间。

abstract.en: Picture a film played one frame at a time until a shape appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影逐格播放，直到出现一个形状。

abstract.en: Picture a seed opening into a map of what it will become.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子打开成一张它将变成什么的图。

examples.en: She read a classic paper in experimental embryology before starting the experiment.
examples.cn: 开始实验之前，她读了一篇实验胚胎学的经典论文。

examples.en: Embryology and genetics now meet in the study of development.
examples.cn: 胚胎学与遗传学如今在发育研究中相遇。

examples.en: The museum's embryology collection includes specimens from a century ago.
examples.cn: 博物馆的胚胎学藏品包括一个世纪前的标本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「embryo 胚胎 + ology 学科」——研究胚胎如何形成的学问 → 胚胎学

root: 希腊 embryon「幼体；肿块」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」+ -logia「研究」，经近代拉丁 embryologia；bryein 更深来源不确定，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline to the development it studies, then to one species, one comparative method, one medical use, one botanical setting, one evolutionary argument and one classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科走向它所研究的发育，再走向单个物种、比较方法、医学用途、植物场景、演化论证与课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of dishes holding one life at successive moments, time laid out side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条摆着玻璃皿的走廊，同一生命的不同瞬间被并排摊开。

branches.en: FIELD AND PROCESS: the study of embryos and the development studied share one name.
branches.cn: 学科与过程：对胚胎的研究与被研究的发育共享一个名称。

branches.en: ONE SPECIES: each organism has its own documented embryonic history.
branches.cn: 单个物种：每种生物都有自己记录在案的胚胎史。

branches.en: COMPARISON: embryos placed side by side become evidence of relatedness.
branches.cn: 比较：并排摆放的胚胎成为亲缘关系的证据。

branches.en: APPLIED SETTINGS: hospitals and seed banks ask different embryological questions.
branches.cn: 应用场景：医院与种子库提出不同的胚胎学问题。

branches.en: ARGUMENT AND LESSON: the field supplies both an evolutionary argument and a course.
branches.cn: 论证与课程：这门学科既提供演化论证，也提供一门课程。

intro.en: Embryology is a Greek compound of a noun about young life and a suffix about study, and both pieces recur across biology.
intro.cn: embryology 是一个希腊复合词，由指幼体生命的名词与指研究的后缀构成，两个部件在生物学中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Greek embryon gives embryo and embryonic; Greek -logia, from logos, gives the names of disciplines such as embryology and histology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 embryon 给出 embryo 与 embryonic；希腊 -logia 出自 logos，给出 embryology、histology 等学科名。

items.example: The prefix places the growing thing inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把生长之物置于内部。

items.example: The verb gives the image of swelling life.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出生命膨胀的意象。
embryon 变成拉丁 embryo。
这个后缀命名一门学科。
embryologia 变成英语 embryology。
胚胎学追踪细胞的路径。

items.example: The embryo has a tiny root.
items.exampleCN: 这个胚胎有一条微小的根。
胚胎组织被取样。
胚胎学家对标本作了分期。

definition_zh: 胚胎的；胚胎期的；萌芽阶段的；未发育完全的
definition_en: relating to an embryo, or existing at a very early stage of development
core_image: 一枚半透明的小标本里，心脏的位置只是一个正在跳动的细点
scene: 在解剖课上，讲师举起一枚很小的标本说：The embryonic heart is already beating at this stage.
sceneCN: 这里 embryonic 指「属于胚胎期的」（第 1 个义项：与胚胎有关的）；句意是在这个阶段，胚胎的心脏已经在跳动。

pos.zh: 萌芽阶段的；未发育完全的

forms.label: 形容词异体（生物学术语）

derivatives.zh: 在胚胎阶段；萌芽状态地

senses.title: Relating to an embryo
senses.titleCN: 与胚胎有关的
senses.definition: relating to or belonging to an embryo
senses.definitionCN: 与胚胎有关或属于胚胎的
senses.example: The embryonic heart is already beating at this stage.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个阶段，胚胎的心脏已经在跳动。
senses.why: Embryo plus -ic makes a plain relational adjective: whatever belongs to the embryo is embryonic.
senses.whyCN: embryo 加 -ic 构成普通的关系形容词：属于胚胎的即为 embryonic。

senses.title: At a very early stage
senses.titleCN: 处于极早期阶段
senses.definition: existing at the earliest stage of development
senses.definitionCN: 处于发育的最早阶段
senses.example: The project is still embryonic and has no budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目仍处于萌芽阶段，还没有预算。
senses.why: Because an embryo is the beginning of an organism, the adjective extends to anything just beginning.
senses.whyCN: 因为胚胎是生物体的开端，这个形容词便延伸到任何刚刚开始的事物。

senses.title: Undeveloped or rudimentary
senses.titleCN: 尚未发育完全的
senses.definition: present only in an undeveloped or rudimentary form
senses.definitionCN: 仅以未发育或退化形式存在的
senses.example: The fish has embryonic pelvic fins that never grow.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼有从未长大的胚胎期腹鳍。
senses.why: A structure caught at the embryonic stage stays small, so the adjective marks something that has not matured.
senses.whyCN: 停留在胚胎阶段的结构保持很小，因此这个形容词标记尚未成熟之物。

senses.title: Relating to embryonic development
senses.titleCN: 与胚胎发育过程有关的
senses.definition: concerning the process by which an embryo develops
senses.definitionCN: 与胚胎发育的过程有关的
senses.example: Embryonic development is studied day by day in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎发育在实验室中被逐日研究。
senses.why: The adjective can modify the process itself, not only the organism, naming the whole sequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可修饰过程本身，而不仅修饰生物体，命名整条序列。

senses.title: Relating to embryonic stem cells
senses.titleCN: 与胚胎干细胞有关的
senses.definition: relating to stem cells taken from an early embryo
senses.definitionCN: 与取自早期胚胎的干细胞有关的
senses.example: Embryonic stem cells can become many kinds of tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎干细胞可以变成许多种组织。
senses.why: Laboratory science fixes the adjective to a cell type, where early-stage origin is the defining property.
senses.whyCN: 实验室科学把这个形容词固定到一种细胞类型上，其早期来源正是定义性特征。

senses.title: Relating to embryonic structures in anatomy
senses.titleCN: 解剖学中与胚胎结构有关的
senses.definition: relating to structures inherited from embryonic anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 与从胚胎解剖继承下来的结构有关的
senses.example: The embryonic gill arches reappear as parts of the adult throat.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎期鳃弓在成体中重现为喉部的一部分。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy keeps the adjective for structures whose origin lies in the embryo even after they change form.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学保留这个形容词，用于那些虽已变形但来源在胚胎的结构。

senses.title: An industry or market at an early stage
senses.titleCN: 处于早期阶段的产业或市场
senses.definition: newly formed and not yet established, said of an industry or market
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚形成、尚未站稳的，用于产业或市场
senses.example: The embryonic industry depends on a single supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 这个初创产业依赖单一供应商。
senses.why: Business writing borrows the biological timeline: young firms are embryonic before they mature.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作借用了生物学时间线：年轻企业在成熟之前处于胚胎期。

senses.title: A plan or idea in its first form
senses.titleCN: 处于最初形态的计划或想法
senses.definition: existing only as an early outline or first conception
senses.definitionCN: 仅以早期提纲或最初构想存在的
senses.example: The design was embryonic, no more than a sketch on a napkin.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计还在雏形阶段，不过是餐巾纸上的一幅草图。
senses.why: The adjective lets a speaker say that an idea has begun but is nowhere near finished.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让说话者表示一个想法已经开始，但远未完成。

intro.en: Embryonic is embryo plus the adjective suffix -ic, which goes back through Latin -icus to Greek -ikos; the word describes whatever belongs to the early forming stage.
intro.cn: embryonic 是 embryo 加形容词后缀 -ic，该后缀经拉丁 -icus 上溯希腊 -ikos；这个词描述属于早期形成阶段的事物。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one still forming, built from en- in and bryein to swell.
items.cn: embryon 意为仍在形成的幼体，由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成。

items.en: Latin embryo carried the Greek noun into scientific Latin, where it named the unborn young.
items.cn: 拉丁 embryo 把这个希腊名词带入科学拉丁语，指未出生的幼体。

items.en: The Greek adjective suffix -ikos, through Latin -icus and French -ique, became English -ic.
items.cn: 希腊形容词后缀 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 变成英语 -ic。

items.en: English embryo appeared in the sixteenth century, and the adjective followed in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语 embryo 在 16 世纪出现，形容词随后在科学写作中出现。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective was applied to industries, plans and ideas at an early stage.
items.cn: 到 19 与 20 世纪，这个形容词被用于早期阶段的产业、计划与想法。

items.era: UNCERTAIN DETAILS (DATE APPROXIMATE, BRYEIN ROOT UNCERTAIN)
items.en: Source uncertain in detail: the first date of the English adjective is approximate, and the deeper root of bryein is unresolved, so any Indo-European base is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源在细节上不确定：英语形容词首见年代为约数，bryein 的更深词根尚无定论，凡给出的印欧语基均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same embryo root; group two holds adjectives describing early or undeveloped states.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词根的各种形式；第二组是描述早期或未发育状态的形容词。

entries.definition: The developing organism; the adjective embryonic describes what belongs to it or what resembles its stage.
entries.definitionCN: 发育中的生物体；形容词 embryonic 描述属于它的或类似其阶段的事物。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective used mostly for embryonic tissue in technical writing; it does not carry the figurative senses.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的形容词，主要用于技术文本中的胚胎组织；不带引申义。

entries.definition: The study of embryos; it names a discipline, not a stage or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的学科；它指学科，而非阶段或性质。

entries.definition: A specialist in embryos; the person noun cannot describe a heart or an industry.
entries.definitionCN: 胚胎专家；指人的名词不能描述心脏或产业。

entries.definition: Relating to a fetus, the stage after the embryonic period; the two adjectives mark successive phases.
entries.definitionCN: 与胎儿有关，即胚胎期之后的阶段；两个形容词标记相继的阶段。

entries.definition: Existing in a basic or imperfect form; it stresses incompleteness rather than the embryo specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 以基本或不完善的形式存在；强调不完整，而非特指胚胎。

entries.definition: Beginning to form or exist; it is a general word for the earliest stage, without a biological image.
entries.definitionCN: 刚开始形成或存在；是泛指最早阶段的词，不含生物意象。

entries.definition: Not fully grown or developed; it may imply delay, while embryonic simply marks an early stage.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未长成或发育完全；可能暗示延迟，而 embryonic 只标记早期阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Embryo plus -ic: belonging to the forming young.
normal.cn: embryo 加 -ic：属于正在形成的幼体。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryology, embryologist, embryonal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryology、embryologist、 embryonal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: embryonic development, stem cell, stage, tissue.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：胚胎发育、胚胎干细胞、胚胎阶段、胚胎组织。

normal.en: The word marks a timeline: embryonic comes before fetal.
normal.cn: 这个词标记时间线：胚胎期在胎儿期之前。

normal.en: Business and design borrow it for anything just starting.
normal.cn: 商业与设计借用它指任何刚刚开始的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a translucent specimen in which the heart is a single pulsing dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚半透明标本，心脏只是一个跳动的细点。

abstract.en: Picture a sketch on a napkin that might become a building.
abstract.cn: 想象餐巾纸上的一幅草图，将来可能变成一栋建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that has split but has no leaves yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒已经裂开却还没有叶子的种子。

examples.en: Embryonic cells were cultured under controlled conditions.
examples.cn: 胚胎细胞在受控条件下培养。

examples.en: The plan remains embryonic and may change entirely.
examples.cn: 这个计划仍处雏形，可能彻底改变。

examples.en: An embryonic trait can persist into adulthood in some species.
examples.cn: 在某些物种中，胚胎期性状可以保留到成体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「embryo 胚胎 + ic 形容词」——属于胚胎阶段的 → 胚胎的、萌芽的

root: embryo + -ic（希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus）；embryo 出自希腊 embryon「幼体」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」；bryein 更深词根不确定，形容词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one timeline: whatever belongs to the earliest forming stage, in a body, a cell, a structure, an industry or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一条时间线：凡属于最早形成阶段的，无论是身体、细胞、结构、产业还是计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny translucent specimen whose heart is only a pulsing point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚半透明的小标本，心脏只是一个跳动的点。

branches.en: EMBRYO STAGE: the adjective marks what belongs to the embryo and to its development.
branches.cn: 胚胎阶段：这个形容词标记属于胚胎及其发育的事物。

branches.en: EARLY MARKET: an industry is embryonic before it matures.
branches.cn: 早期市场：产业在成熟之前处于胚胎状态。

branches.en: RUDIMENT: a structure may stay embryonic even in an adult body.
branches.cn: 退化或雏形：某结构即使在成体中也可能保持胚胎状态。

branches.en: CELL POTENTIAL: embryonic stem cells carry the widest range of possible futures.
branches.cn: 细胞潜能：胚胎干细胞携带最广的可能未来。

branches.en: INCOMPLETENESS: the word warns that something is begun but not finished.
branches.cn: 不完整：这个词提示某事已开始但尚未完成。

intro.en: Embryonic is a Greek-derived noun plus a Greek-derived adjective suffix, and the same suffix builds hundreds of English adjectives.
intro.cn: embryonic 是一个希腊来源的名词加一个希腊来源的形容词后缀，同一后缀构成数百个英语形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek embryon supplies the noun; Greek -ikos, through Latin -icus and French -ique, supplies the ending -ic seen in embryonic, organic and cosmic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 embryon 提供名词；希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 提供 -ic 词尾，见于 embryonic、organic、cosmic。

items.example: The prefix places growth inside a container.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把生长置于容器内部。

items.example: The verb gives the image of swelling life.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出生命膨胀的意象。

items.example: Embryon passed into Latin as embryo.
items.exampleCN: embryon 以 embryo 进入拉丁语。

items.example: The embryo has a tiny root.
items.exampleCN: 这个胚胎有一条微小的根。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。
胚胎组织被取样。
该器官在胚胎期发育。
胚胎性肿瘤很罕见。
胚胎学解释这一序列。

definition_en: the unborn or newly developing young of an organism, or the earliest form of something
core_image: 一粒种子被切开，里面蜷着一条极小的根与芽，整个未来的植株已经按比例缩小藏在这里
scene: 在植物实验室里，技术员切开一枚种子说：The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
sceneCN: 这里 embryo 指「种子内处于早期发育阶段的胚」（第 3 个义项：植物种子中的胚）；句意是种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。
