senses.title: The developing young of an animal
senses.titleCN: 动物发育中的幼体
senses.definition: the unborn or newly developing young of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 动物未出生或刚发育的幼体
senses.example: The embryo implants in the womb about a week after fertilization.
senses.exampleCN: 受精约一周后，胚胎着床于子宫。
senses.why: Greek embryon named the young one still forming inside, so the noun points at the organism before it has taken shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 embryon 指在里面仍在形成的幼体，因此这个名词指尚未成形时的生物体。

senses.title: A human embryo in its early stage
senses.titleCN: 早期阶段的人类胚胎
senses.definition: a human organism in the first weeks after fertilization
senses.definitionCN: 受精后最初数周的人类生物体
senses.example: The human embryo is called a fetus after the eighth week.
senses.exampleCN: 人类胚胎在第八周之后被称为胎儿。
senses.why: Medicine needs a boundary, so embryo marks the early weeks before the fetal stage begins.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一条界线，因此 embryo 标记胎儿阶段开始之前的最初数周。

senses.title: The plant embryo inside a seed
senses.titleCN: 种子内部的植物胚
senses.definition: the young plant contained within a seed
senses.definitionCN: 包含在种子内的幼小植株
senses.example: The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
senses.exampleCN: 种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。
senses.why: Plants package the young plant inside a seed, and botany uses the same noun for that dormant form.
senses.whyCN: 植物把幼株包在种子里，植物学用同一个名词指这种休眠形态。

senses.title: The earliest form of something
senses.titleCN: 事物的最初形态
senses.definition: the beginning or germ of something that will develop further
senses.definitionCN: 将进一步发展之物的开端或雏形
senses.example: The first sketch was the embryo of the finished building.
senses.exampleCN: 第一幅草图是这座建成建筑的前身。
senses.why: Because an embryo contains the whole future in miniature, the noun extends to any early germ of a larger thing.
senses.whyCN: 因为胚胎以缩小的形式包含整个未来，这个名词便延伸到任何较大事物的早期雏形。

senses.title: An embryo in assisted reproduction
senses.titleCN: 辅助生殖中的胚胎
senses.definition: an embryo produced and transferred in fertility treatment
senses.definitionCN: 生育治疗中培育并移植的胚胎
senses.example: The clinic transferred one embryo and froze the others.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所移植了一个胚胎，把其余的冷冻起来。
senses.why: Reproductive technology makes the embryo an object handled outside the body, giving the noun a clinical sense.
senses.whyCN: 生殖技术使胚胎成为在体外被操作的对象，使这个名词获得临床义。

senses.title: An embryo as a specimen
senses.titleCN: 作为研究标本的胚胎
senses.definition: a preserved or staged embryo used for study
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究而保存或分期的胚胎
senses.example: The collection holds embryos at every stage of development.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品保存着每个发育阶段的胚胎。
senses.why: In a laboratory the embryo becomes a specimen with a stage number, a thing to be compared rather than a future animal.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，胚胎变成带分期编号的标本，是被比较的对象，而非未来的动物。

senses.title: The embryo contrasted with the larva
senses.titleCN: 与幼虫相对的胚胎
senses.definition: the developmental stage before hatching, as distinct from a free-living larva
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之前的发育阶段，与自由生活的幼虫相对
senses.example: The embryo develops inside the egg before the larva emerges.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎在卵内发育，之后幼虫才出来。
senses.why: Zoology separates stages by whether the young is still enclosed, and embryo marks the enclosed phase.
senses.whyCN: 动物学按幼体是否仍被包裹来划分阶段，embryo 标记被包裹的阶段。

senses.title: The germ of a plan or design
senses.titleCN: 计划或设计的最初构想
senses.definition: an early idea from which a plan or work may grow
senses.definitionCN: 计划或作品可能由此生长的最初想法
senses.example: The idea remained an embryo for years before anyone funded it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法多年只是雏形，直到有人资助。
senses.why: The biological image gives the noun a figurative life: a plan can be pregnant with a future it has not yet shown.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象给这个名词以比喻生命：一个计划可以孕育着尚未显露的未来。

intro.en: Embryo comes from Greek embryon, a young one still forming, built from en- in and bryein to swell; Latin and English adopted it as a scientific noun.
intro.cn: embryo 来自希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体」，由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成；拉丁语与英语把它作为科学名词吸收。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one, and also a swelling; the word pictured life growing inside a enclosing body.
items.cn: embryon 意为幼体，也指肿块；这个词描绘生命在有包裹的身体内生长。

items.en: En- meant in and bryein meant to swell or be full; the compound's literal sense is swelling within.
items.cn: en- 意为「在内」，bryein 意为「膨胀、充满」；复合词的字面义是「在里面膨胀」。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as embryo and used it in learned writing for the unborn young.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这一希腊名词吸收为 embryo，在学术写作中指未出生的幼体。

items.en: English embryo appeared in the sixteenth century, first in learned and medical contexts.
items.cn: 英语 embryo 在 16 世纪出现，最初用于学术与医学语境。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun was also used for the early form of a thing, a usage that persists in modern writing.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，这个名词也用于指事物的早期形态，这一用法在现代写作中延续。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of bryein is not established, so any Indo-European base offered is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（bryein 词根存疑、年代为约数）：bryein 的更深来源未得到证明，凡为其给出的印欧语基均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same embryo stock; group two holds stages and near terms in developmental biology.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词族的词；第二组是发育生物学中的阶段与近义术语。

entries.definition: Relating to an embryo or to an early stage; it describes, while embryo names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚胎或早期阶段有关的形容词；它作描述，而 embryo 指对象。

entries.definition: The study of embryos; it names a science, not the organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的学科；它指科学，而非生物体。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective for embryonic tissue, used mainly in pathology and anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的形容词，指胚胎组织，主要用于病理学与解剖学。

entries.definition: The nourishing tissue inside a seed; it surrounds the plant embryo but is not the embryo itself.
entries.definitionCN: 种子内提供营养的组织；它包围植物胚，但本身不是胚。

entries.definition: The unborn young after the embryonic stage; the two nouns mark successive phases.
entries.definitionCN: 胚胎阶段之后未出生的幼体；两个名词标记相继阶段。

entries.definition: An independent young form that hatches and feeds itself, unlike an embryo still enclosed.
entries.definitionCN: 孵化后独立取食的幼体形态，与仍被包裹的胚胎不同。

entries.definition: The structure that holds the plant embryo with its food supply; the embryo is inside the seed.
entries.definitionCN: 包含植物胚与养分供应的结构；胚在种子内部。

entries.definition: The earliest stage from which something may develop; it is the figurative counterpart of embryo.
entries.definitionCN: 某物可能由此发展的最早阶段；是 embryo 的比喻对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: En- in plus bryein swell: life swelling inside a wrapping.
normal.cn: en-「在内」加 bryein「膨胀」：生命在包裹内膨胀。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryonic, embryology, embryologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryonic、embryology、embryologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: human embryo, plant embryo, embryo transfer, embryo sac.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类胚胎、植物胚、胚胎移植、胚囊。

normal.en: The timeline is embryo, then fetus, then birth.
normal.cn: 时间线是胚胎、胎儿、出生。

normal.en: In seeds the embryo waits, tiny but complete in outline.
normal.cn: 在种子里，胚静静等待，微小却轮廓完整。

abstract.en: Picture a seed cut open to reveal a miniature plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被切开，露出一株缩小的植株。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint folded small enough to fit in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图折得小到能放进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a whole tree sleeping inside one hard shell.
abstract.cn: 想象整棵树睡在一枚硬壳里。

examples.en: The embryo divides rapidly in the first days after fertilization.
examples.cn: 受精后的最初几天，胚胎迅速分裂。

examples.en: Botanists distinguish the embryo from the surrounding food tissue.
examples.cn: 植物学家把胚与周围的营养组织区分开。

examples.en: The novel was still an embryo when the war began.
examples.cn: 战争开始时，这部小说还只是雏形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em 在内 + bryo 膨胀」——在里面膨胀生长的幼体 → 胚胎、雏形

root: 希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体；肿块」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」，经拉丁 embryo 进入英语；bryein 更深词根不确定，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one noun from an animal's developing young to a human stage, a seed's plant, a figurative germ, a clinical object, a museum specimen, a zoological phase and the first form of a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个名词从动物发育中的幼体走向人类阶段、种子里的植株、比喻的雏形、临床对象、博物馆标本、动物学阶段，最后走向计划的最初形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed opened to show a tiny plant that already carries the whole future in outline.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒种子被打开，露出一株已以轮廓携带全部未来的小植株。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL YOUNG: animal, human and plant embryos are the same stage in different containers.
branches.cn: 生物学幼体：动物、人类与植物胚是不同容器中的同一阶段。

branches.en: EARLIEST FORM: anything larger begins as an embryo of itself.
branches.cn: 最初形态：任何更大的事物都以自身的胚胎形态开始。

branches.en: OBJECT OF HANDLING: clinics transfer embryos, museums stage them as specimens.
branches.cn: 被操作的对象：诊所移植胚胎，博物馆把它分期为标本。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: the embryo ends where the free-living larva or fetus begins.
branches.cn: 边界：胚胎在自由生活幼虫或胎儿开始处结束。

branches.en: UNREALIZED FUTURE: the noun names something whose future is still folded inside it.
branches.cn: 未实现的未来：这个名词指未来仍折叠在其内部的事物。

intro.en: Embryo is a Greek noun borrowed whole, but its parts can still be read and compared with other scientific words.
intro.cn: embryo 是一个整体借入的希腊名词，但它的部件仍可读出，并与其他科学词比较。

latinIntro.en: Greek en- and bryein build embryon; the same en- appears in endemic and energy, while bryein is rare outside this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 en- 与 bryein 构成 embryon；同一个 en- 见于 endemic 与 energy，而 bryein 在此词族之外很少见。

items.example: The prefix marks something growing inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记在内部生长之物。

items.example: The verb is confined largely to this family in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在英语中基本只限于这个词族。
embryon 以 embryo 进入拉丁语。

items.example: The embryo is enclosed in the seed.
items.exampleCN: 胚被包在种子里。
胚叶是折叠的。
胚胎组织被检查。
胚胎学描述各阶段。
胚胎学家对样本作了分期。
胚乳为胚提供养分。

definition_en: the unborn young of a mammal, especially a human, after the embryonic stage
core_image: 一张产检影像里，一个已经成形的小身体蜷着，手指与脊柱都清晰可辨
scene: 在产检室里，医生指着屏幕说：The fetus is developing normally at twenty weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 fetus 指「胚胎期之后、出生之前的胎儿」（第 2 个义项：人类妊娠八周之后的胎儿）；句意是二十周时胎儿发育正常。

senses.title: The unborn young of a mammal
senses.titleCN: 哺乳动物未出生的幼体
senses.definition: the unborn young of a mammal while it is carried in the womb
senses.definitionCN: 哺乳动物在子宫内孕育时未出生的幼体
senses.example: The fetus receives oxygen through the placenta.
senses.exampleCN: 胎儿通过胎盘获得氧气。
senses.why: Latin fetus named the bearing of young and the offspring itself, so the noun begins as the carried young.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fetus 指「生育、孕育」以及所生后代，因此这个名词最初指被孕育的幼体。

senses.title: A human fetus after the embryonic stage
senses.titleCN: 胚胎期之后的人类胎儿
senses.definition: a human unborn young from about the eighth week until birth
senses.definitionCN: 人类从约第八周到出生前未出生的幼体
senses.example: The fetus is developing normally at twenty weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 二十周时胎儿发育正常。
senses.why: Medicine draws a line at the eighth week, after which the form is recognizably human and the word fetus applies.
senses.whyCN: 医学在第八周划线，此后形态已可辨认为人形，便使用 fetus 一词。

senses.title: An animal fetus
senses.titleCN: 动物的胎儿
senses.definition: the unborn young of a non-human mammal
senses.definitionCN: 非人类哺乳动物未出生的幼体
senses.example: The ultrasound showed a single fetus in the mare.
senses.exampleCN: 超声显示母马体内有一个胎儿。
senses.why: Veterinary work uses the same noun because the biology of carrying young is shared across mammals.
senses.whyCN: 兽医工作使用同一名词，因为孕育幼体的生物学在哺乳动物中相通。

senses.title: The fetus as an object of prenatal diagnosis
senses.titleCN: 作为产前诊断对象的胎儿
senses.definition: the unborn young considered as a patient or subject of medical examination
senses.definitionCN: 作为病人或医学检查对象的未出生幼体
senses.example: The fetus was measured and its heartbeat recorded.
senses.exampleCN: 胎儿被测量，心跳也被记录。
senses.why: Modern medicine treats the fetus as a separate patient, which gives the noun a clinical, measurable sense.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学把胎儿当作独立病人，这赋予该名词临床、可测量的含义。

senses.title: The unborn child in law
senses.titleCN: 法律意义上的未出生子女
senses.definition: the unborn young considered in legal or ethical discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或伦理讨论中被考虑的未出生幼体
senses.example: The law treats the fetus as a potential heir in some jurisdictions.
senses.exampleCN: 在有些司法辖区，法律把胎儿视为可能的继承人。
senses.why: Courts and ethics committees need a term for the unborn that is neither embryo nor child, and fetus fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 法院与伦理委员会需要一个既非胚胎也非儿童的说法，fetus 填补了这个位置。

senses.title: The fetal stage on a timeline
senses.titleCN: 发育时间线上的胎儿期
senses.definition: the stage of development between the embryonic period and birth
senses.definitionCN: 胚胎期与出生之间的发育阶段
senses.example: The fetus stage is marked by growth rather than new organs.
senses.exampleCN: 胎儿期的标志是生长，而非新器官形成。
senses.why: Developmental biology uses the noun as a stage label, a segment on the calendar of gestation.
senses.whyCN: 发育生物学把这个名词用作阶段标签，即妊娠日历上的一段。

senses.title: A preserved fetus specimen
senses.titleCN: 保存的胎儿标本
senses.definition: a preserved unborn young kept for anatomical study
senses.definitionCN: 为解剖研究而保存的未出生幼体
senses.example: The museum holds a fetus from each stage of the pregnancy.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保存着妊娠每个阶段的胎儿。
senses.why: Anatomy collections turn the fetus into a specimen, a reference object rather than a coming person.
senses.whyCN: 解剖收藏把胎儿变成标本，是参照物而非即将出生的人。

senses.title: The fetus in assisted reproduction
senses.titleCN: 辅助生殖语境中的胎儿
senses.definition: the stage reached after a transferred embryo implants and develops
senses.definitionCN: 移植胚胎着床并发育后所达到的阶段
senses.example: After transfer, the embryo became a fetus within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 移植之后，胚胎在数周内成为胎儿。
senses.why: Fertility treatment follows the same timeline, so the noun marks the point where an embryo has safely become a fetus.
senses.whyCN: 生育治疗遵循同一条时间线，因此这个名词标记胚胎安全转为胎儿的节点。

intro.en: Fetus is Latin for the bearing of young and the offspring so carried; the British spelling foetus is a later learned alteration, not the original form.
intro.cn: fetus 是拉丁语，指孕育幼体以及被孕育的后代；英式拼写 foetus 是后来的学术性改动，并非原形。

items.en: Fetus meant the bearing or bringing forth of young, and also the offspring and the pregnancy itself.
items.cn: fetus 指孕育或生产幼体，也指后代以及妊娠本身。

items.en: The Latin noun is linked by some to an Indo-European root *dhe(i)- to suck or suckle, a reconstruction shared with fecund and female; the connection is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词被一些人联系到印欧词根 *dhe(i)-「吸吮」，属重构形式，并与 fecund、female 共享；这一联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The spelling foetus arose in learned writing because a false link to Latin foetere to stink was imagined; fetus is the earlier and etymologically correct form.
items.cn: foetus 这一拼写出现在学术写作中，原因是有人误以为它与拉丁 foetere「发臭」有关；fetus 才是更早且在词源上正确的形式。

items.en: English fetus entered medical writing in the sixteenth century, alongside the adjective fetal.
items.cn: 英语 fetus 于 16 世纪进入医学写作，形容词 fetal 同时出现。

items.en: With ultrasound and prenatal care, the noun became a standard clinical term for the unborn after the embryonic weeks.
items.cn: 随着超声与产前护理，这个名词成为指胚胎期之后未出生幼体的标准临床术语。

items.en: Source uncertain in two ways: the Indo-European root link is a hypothesis, and the first English date is approximate; the Latin noun itself and the foetus spelling history are well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定有两处：印欧词根联系只是假说，英语首见年代为约数；拉丁名词本身与 foetus 拼写史则有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and derivatives of fetus that are easily confused; group two holds near terms for the unborn at different stages.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 fetus 拼写与派生词；第二组是不同阶段未出生幼体的近义术语。

entries.definition: A British variant spelling of fetus, historically a learned alteration; it names the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: fetus 的英式异体拼写，历史上是学术性改动；所指相同。

entries.definition: Relating to a fetus; it describes the stage, while fetus names the organism.
entries.definitionCN: 与胎儿有关的形容词；它描述阶段，而 fetus 指生物体。

entries.definition: Fruitful or fertile, possibly from the same Indo-European root as fetus; the link is reconstructed, not proved.
entries.definitionCN: 多产或肥沃，可能与 fetus 同出同一印欧词根；这一联系属重构，未获证明。

entries.definition: From Latin effetus, worn out by bearing, which does contain fetus; the modern sense is depleted or over-refined.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 effetus「因生育而衰弱」，其中确有 fetus；现代义为衰竭或过度讲究。

entries.definition: The stage before the fetus; the boundary is usually placed at the eighth week in human development.
entries.definitionCN: 胎儿之前的阶段；人类发育中通常以第八周为界。

entries.definition: A human term that stresses personhood rather than developmental stage.
entries.definitionCN: 强调人而非发育阶段的说法。

entries.definition: The whole product of conception, including membranes; the fetus is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 受孕产物的整体，包括胎膜；胎儿是其中一部分。

entries.definition: A newborn, the stage after birth; it begins where the fetus stage ends.
entries.definitionCN: 新生儿，出生后的阶段；它在胎儿阶段结束处开始。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin fetus means bearing and offspring: the carried young.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fetus 指孕育与后代：被孕育的幼体。

normal.en: The family runs fetus, fetal, foetal, fetology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fetus、fetal、foetal、fetology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: human fetus, developing fetus, fetal monitoring.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类胎儿、发育中的胎儿、胎儿监护。

normal.en: The timeline is embryo, fetus, neonate.
normal.cn: 时间线是胚胎、胎儿、新生儿。

normal.en: The British foetus is a later alteration, not the original spelling.
normal.cn: 英式 foetus 是后来的改动，并非原拼写。

abstract.en: Picture a scan in which a curled body shows fingers and spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张影像，蜷起的小身体显出指头与脊柱。

abstract.en: Picture a passenger already aboard, waiting for the door to open.
abstract.cn: 想象一位已经上船的乘客，等着门打开。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that has grown too large for its shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒长得超出外壳的种子。

examples.en: The fetus can hear sounds from outside the womb by the third trimester.
examples.cn: 到第三孕期，胎儿已能听见子宫外的声音。

examples.en: Researchers studied how the fetus responds to maternal stress.
examples.cn: 研究者研究了胎儿如何回应母体应激。

examples.en: The museum's collection includes a fetus preserved in fluid.
examples.cn: 博物馆的藏品包括一个保存在液体中的胎儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fetus 孕育」——被孕育在体内的幼体 → 胎儿

root: 拉丁 fetus「孕育；后代；妊娠」；其印欧词根联系（*dhe(i)-「吸吮」）属重构假说。英式 foetus 为后来学术性改动。英语首见年代约 16 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one noun on a timeline: the carried young, the human stage after the eighth week, the animal case, the clinical patient, the legal subject, the developmental stage, the museum specimen and the post-transfer stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个名词留在一条时间线上：被孕育的幼体、第八周后的人类阶段、动物情形、临床病人、法律主体、发育阶段、博物馆标本与移植后的阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an image of a curled, already formed body waiting inside the womb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张影像，一个已经成形、蜷着等待的身体在子宫内。

branches.en: CARRIED YOUNG: the noun begins with the mammal's unborn young.
branches.cn: 被孕育的幼体：这个名词从哺乳动物未出生的幼体开始。

branches.en: HUMAN TIMELINE: the eighth week marks the shift from embryo to fetus.
branches.cn: 人类时间线：第八周标记从胚胎到胎儿的转换。

branches.en: CLINICAL OBJECT: ultrasound turns the fetus into something measured and monitored.
branches.cn: 临床对象：超声把胎儿变成可测量、可监护的对象。

branches.en: LEGAL SUBJECT: courts need a term for the unborn that is not simply child.
branches.cn: 法律主体：法院需要一个不单纯等于「孩子」的未出生者称谓。

branches.en: SPECIMEN AND OUTCOME: a fetus can be studied in a jar or awaited after transfer.
branches.cn: 标本与结果：胎儿可被保存在罐中研究，也可在移植后被等待。

intro.en: Fetus is a Latin noun borrowed whole; its family is small, and the spelling history is as important as the morphology.
intro.cn: fetus 是一个整体借入的拉丁名词；词族较小，而拼写史与形态学同样重要。

latinIntro.en: Latin fetus gives fetal and fetology; the Greek-derived embryo belongs to a different root, though the two words share a timeline.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fetus 衍生 fetal 与 fetology；希腊来源的 embryo 属另一词根，尽管两词共享一条时间线。

items.example: Fetus named both the process and the offspring.
items.exampleCN: fetus 同时指过程与后代。
胎儿生长被测量。

items.meaningCN: 与胎儿有关的（英式拼写）
items.exampleCN: 胎儿监护持续整夜。

items.example: The British journal still prints foetus.
items.exampleCN: 这家英国期刊仍印作 foetus。
胎儿学与产科学有重叠。
法律单独讨论杀胎问题。
胚胎在胎儿之前。

items.example: The neonate was examined at once.
items.exampleCN: 新生儿立即接受检查。

definition_zh: 妊娠期；孕育过程；（想法、作品的）酝酿期
definition_en: the period or process of carrying young in the womb, or a period of development before something is produced
core_image: 一块记着日期的木牌挂在栏边，从配种那天到生产那天，中间是一段被等待填满的时间
scene: 在动物园的饲养记录里，管理员写下日期后说：Gestation in this species lasts about eleven months.
sceneCN: 这里 gestation 指「从受孕到生产的妊娠期长度」（第 3 个义项：妊娠持续时间）；句意是这个物种的妊娠期约为十一个月。

senses.title: The carrying of young in the womb
senses.titleCN: 在子宫内孕育幼体的过程
senses.definition: the process of carrying a developing young inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 在体内携带发育中幼体的过程
senses.example: Gestation begins with implantation and ends with birth.
senses.exampleCN: 妊娠从着床开始，到出生结束。
senses.why: Gestare means to carry, so gestation is literally the carrying of young, the process rather than the count of days.
senses.whyCN: gestare 意为「携带」，因此 gestation 字面就是携带幼体，指过程而非天数。

senses.title: Pregnancy as a state
senses.titleCN: 作为状态的妊娠
senses.definition: the state of being pregnant
senses.definitionCN: 怀孕的状态
senses.example: Nutrition during gestation affects the young's later health.
senses.exampleCN: 妊娠期间的营养影响幼体日后的健康。
senses.why: The process can also be viewed as a condition a body is in, so the noun names the state as well.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程也可视为身体所处的一种状态，因此这个名词也指状态。

senses.title: The length of pregnancy
senses.titleCN: 妊娠持续时间
senses.definition: the period from conception to birth, measured in days or weeks
senses.definitionCN: 从受孕到出生的时间，以日或周计
senses.example: Gestation in this species lasts about eleven months.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的妊娠期约为十一个月。
senses.why: Once measured, the carrying process becomes a duration, and the noun names the number of days.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被测量，孕育过程就变成一个时长，这个名词便指天数。

senses.title: Animal gestation
senses.titleCN: 动物的妊娠
senses.definition: the carrying period of a non-human animal
senses.definitionCN: 非人类动物的孕育期
senses.example: Elephant gestation is among the longest of any land mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 大象的妊娠期是陆生哺乳动物中最长的之一。
senses.why: The same biological process receives the same noun across mammals, with the length varying by species.
senses.whyCN: 同一生物过程在不同哺乳动物中用同一名词，长度随物种而变。

senses.title: The incubation of an idea
senses.titleCN: 想法的酝酿期
senses.definition: the period during which an idea or plan develops before it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 想法或计划在呈现之前的发展时期
senses.example: The proposal had a long gestation before it reached the board.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案在送到董事会之前经历了漫长的酝酿。
senses.why: An idea is pictured as being carried unseen, exactly as a body carries young, until it is ready to be born.
senses.whyCN: 想法被想象为被看不见地携带，正像身体携带幼体，直到可以出生。

senses.title: Internal development in viviparous animals
senses.titleCN: 胎生动物体内的发育
senses.definition: development inside the mother's body rather than in an egg
senses.definitionCN: 在母体内而非卵内的发育
senses.example: Viviparity extends gestation beyond the egg stage.
senses.exampleCN: 胎生使孕育延伸到卵阶段之后。
senses.why: Zoology uses the noun to mark the internal route of development, contrasted with laying eggs.
senses.whyCN: 动物学用这个名词标记体内发育路径，与产卵相对。

senses.title: Gestational age in obstetrics
senses.titleCN: 产科中的孕龄
senses.definition: the age of a pregnancy measured from the last menstrual period
senses.definitionCN: 从末次月经起算的妊娠时长
senses.example: Gestation is counted from the last menstrual period, not from conception.
senses.exampleCN: 孕龄从末次月经起算，而非从受孕起算。
senses.why: Clinical practice needs a fixed starting point, so the noun becomes a measurement convention.
senses.whyCN: 临床实践需要固定起点，这个名词于是成为一种测量约定。

senses.title: The incubation of a work of art
senses.titleCN: 艺术作品的酝酿期
senses.definition: the period in which a work or project is formed before it appears
senses.definitionCN: 作品或项目在问世之前形成的时期
senses.example: The novel's gestation took a decade of notes and revisions.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的酝酿花了十年笔记与修改。
senses.why: Creative work also ripens unseen, and the biological metaphor gives that invisible period a name.
senses.whyCN: 创作也在看不见处成熟，生物比喻给这段不可见时期一个名称。

intro.en: Gestation comes from Latin gestatio, a carrying, from gestare to carry, a frequentative of gerere to carry or bear; the deeper origin of gerere is uncertain.
intro.cn: gestation 来自拉丁 gestatio「携带」，出自 gestare「携带」，后者是 gerere「携带、承担」的反复动词；gerere 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Gerere meant to carry, bear or manage; its deeper origin is not established, and the many senses of the English descendants reflect that breadth.
items.cn: gerere 意为携带、承担、管理；其更深来源未得到证明，英语后裔的多种词义正反映这种宽度。

items.en: Gestare was a frequentative of gerere, meaning to carry about or keep carrying, which suits the long carrying of young.
items.cn: gestare 是 gerere 的反复动词，意为「反复携带、带在身上」，正合长期孕育幼体。

items.en: Gestatio named a carrying or being carried, and in medical Latin the carrying of young in the womb.
items.cn: gestatio 指携带或被携带，在医学拉丁语中指在子宫内孕育幼体。

items.en: English gestation appeared in the early seventeenth century, first for the carrying of young and soon after for the period itself.
items.cn: 英语 gestation 在 17 世纪初出现，先指孕育幼体，随后很快指这一时期本身。

items.en: Later writers applied the word to the slow formation of ideas, books and projects.
items.cn: 后来的作者把这个词用于想法、书籍与项目的缓慢形成。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of Latin gerere is unresolved, so any Indo-European base offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（gerere 词根存疑、年代为约数）：拉丁 gerere 的更深来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语基均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin carrying root that are easily confused; group two holds terms for pregnancy and for slow formation.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「携带」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是妊娠与缓慢形成的近义术语。

entries.definition: To carry young or develop an idea; the verb is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 孕育幼体或酝酿想法；动词是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: Relating to gestation, especially to age or diabetes in pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 与妊娠有关的，尤指孕龄或妊娠期糖尿病。

entries.definition: From gestus, a bearing or movement of the body, also from gerere; it shares the root but means a movement, not a carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 gestus「身体的姿态或动作」，同样出自 gerere；共享词根，但指动作而非携带。

entries.definition: From digerere, to carry apart or dissolve, built on the same gerere; it distributes rather than carries young.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 digerere「分开运送、消解」，同出 gerere；它是分解分配，而非孕育。

entries.definition: The condition of carrying young; it names the state more plainly than gestation, which often names the period.
entries.definitionCN: 携带幼体的状态；比 gestation 更直白地指状态，而 gestation 常指时期。

entries.definition: Sitting on eggs or, figuratively, letting something develop; it is the closest word for the idea sense.
entries.definitionCN: 孵卵，或比喻让某物发展；是「想法」义最接近的词。

entries.definition: The medical state of being pregnant, from Latin gravis heavy; it is a clinical synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 怀孕的医学状态，来自拉丁 gravis「重」；是临床近义词。

entries.definition: The length of a pregnancy, as in full term; it names the measured span that gestation can also denote.
entries.definitionCN: 妊娠的长度，如足月；它指 gestation 也可表示的测量时长。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Gestare to carry plus -tion: the carrying of young.
normal.cn: gestare「携带」加 -tion：携带幼体。

normal.en: The family runs gestate, gestation, gestational, gestationally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gestate、gestation、gestational、gestationally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: gestation period, length of gestation, during gestation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：妊娠期、妊娠时长、妊娠期间。

normal.en: The verb gestate also covers ideas and books.
normal.cn: 动词 gestate 也涵盖想法与书。

normal.en: Same root, different branches: gesture and digestion.
normal.cn: 同根不同枝：gesture 与 digestion。

abstract.en: Picture a dated board by a pen, counting days from mating to birth.
abstract.cn: 想象栏边一块记日期的牌子，从配种数到生产。

abstract.en: Picture a manuscript carried unseen for ten years before it opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手稿被看不见地携带十年才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a pot on a low flame that must not be hurried.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小火上的锅，急不得。

examples.en: Elephant gestation lasts nearly two years.
examples.cn: 大象的妊娠期接近两年。

examples.en: The policy had a long gestation and many drafts.
examples.cn: 这项政策经历了漫长的酝酿与许多草案。

examples.en: Gestational diabetes is usually tested for late in the second trimester.
examples.cn: 妊娠期糖尿病通常在第二孕期后期筛查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gest 携带 + ation 过程」——把幼体带在身上的一段时间 → 妊娠期、酝酿期

root: 拉丁 gestatio「携带」← gestare「携带」（gerere「携带、承担」的反复动词）；gerere 更深来源不确定，英语首见年代约 17 世纪初。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one carrying: the process, the state, the measured length, the animal case, the incubation of an idea, internal development, clinical dating and the ripening of a work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「携带」展开：过程、状态、测得的时长、动物情形、想法酝酿、体内发育、临床计时与作品成熟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dated board counting the days between mating and birth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块记日期的牌子，数着配种到生产的每一天。

branches.en: PREGNANCY STATE: carrying young is also a condition one is in.
branches.cn: 妊娠状态：孕育幼体也是一种持续所处的状态。

branches.en: MEASURED TIME: days, species differences and clinical starting points turn carrying into a number.
branches.cn: 被测量的时间：天数、物种差异与临床起点把孕育变成数字。

branches.en: IDEA INCUBATION: a plan is carried unseen until it is ready.
branches.cn: 想法的酝酿：计划在被看见之前一直默默孕育。

branches.en: INTERNAL ROUTE: gestation marks development inside the body rather than in an egg.
branches.cn: 体内路径：gestation 标记体内发育而非卵内发育。

branches.en: HELD INSIDE: from a child to a work, something is carried before it appears.
branches.cn: 内含之孕：从胎儿到作品，都是先被孕育再被呈现。

intro.en: Gestation is a Latin frequentative verb turned into a noun, and the same carrying root builds several words with very different meanings.
intro.cn: gestation 是一个拉丁反复动词变来的名词，同一个「携带」词根构成若干意义很不同的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere gives gestare, gestation, gesture and digestion; the frequentative gestare adds the sense of repeated or sustained carrying.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gerere 衍生 gestare、gestation、gesture 与 digestion；反复动词 gestare 增添「反复或持续携带」之义。

items.example: The verb is the base of a wide family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是一个大词族的基础。

items.example: Gestare supplied the idea of sustained carrying.
items.exampleCN: gestare 提供持续携带的观念。

items.example: Gestatio entered medical Latin for pregnancy.
items.exampleCN: gestatio 以妊娠义进入医学拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。
这里的妊娠期持续十一个月。
这个计划酝酿了多年。
孕龄被记录下来。

items.example: A gesture can carry meaning without words.
items.exampleCN: 手势可以不靠言语携带意义。
消化把食物变成养分。
